Miller tallied 19 yards on six touches during the Week 3 loss, playing behind both Alvin Kamara and Etienne. As Etienne deals with an ongoing hamstring injury, Miller is likely to split work on the ground with Kamara in the Week 4 contest, operating as one of the Saints' leading rushers. Despite this, Miller is in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that's allowed just 3.1 yards per carry this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kirk Cousins had a bumpy Raiders debut in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, completing 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. The veteran quarterback is just keeping the starting job warm for 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but the team is in no hurry to get the rookie in the lineup before he's ready, and wins will only give Cousins more job security. His passing numbers could improve once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to play, as his most productive connection was running back Ashton Jeanty, who was on the other end of two of Cousins' TD passes. Cousins will face a Chargers defense in Week 2 that had trouble slowing down Jacoby Brissett in its opener but finished fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kirk Cousins is having a late-season renaissance with the Raiders. The 38-year-old quarterback has thrown exactly three touchdown passes in each of the first three games of the season, leading his new team to a 3-0 record and keeping first overall pick Fernando Mendoza firmly on the bench. Cousins has also thrown three INTs, and those mistakes could catch up against tougher competition, as two of those victories have come against the NFL's five remaining winless squads. On the other hand, that production came despite Brock Bowers missing the first two weeks, and the star tight end erupted for a 10-116-1 line in his Week 3 debut. Cousins will get his first real test of the year in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will work as the team's starter to open the 2026 season ahead of No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenton Strange was one of four Jaguars to catch a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence in the season-opening win over the Browns, and the starting tight end should remain involved in the Week 2 game plan against the Broncos. The Broncos excelled at defending wide receivers last season but gave up the ninth-most receiving yards to TEs. Strange is a decent fantasy option in multi-TE formats or those with a tight end premium. However, with many mouths to feed in Jacksonville's passing game, Strange is tough to trust as a starter in standard single-TE leagues. Strange has exceeded 61 receiving yards just once since the start of last season while scoring four TDs in 13 appearances over that span.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brenton Strange remains a complementary piece in Jacksonville's passing game heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. He's locked in atop the Jaguars' TE depth chart, but Strange has just seven catches for 72 yards and a TD on 10 targets in three games-numbers elite options at his position often reach in one game. The Bengals have allowed 23 catches (third-most) and 299 yards (second-most) to TEs, so Strange has more fantasy appeal than usual in Week 4 and is a viable option in multi-TE or TE-premium formats. Even the favorable matchup isn't enough to propel him into the starting range in most one-TE leagues.

player.seasonOutlook: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Holani looks set as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Cardinals. Holani somewhat surprisingly logged eight carries in a tight Week 1 win over the Patriots, recording only two fewer totes than rookie Jadarian Price. However, Price was much more efficient with 5.2 YPC to Holani's 3.6. Price could get a larger share of the workload against the Cardinals, who limited the Chargers to 81 rushing yards on 21 carries in a season-opening victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Holani may be asked to take on a bigger offensive role for Seattle in a Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury late in a Week 2 win against Arizona, and if he isn't able to suit up versus Washington, Holani would figure to see more work, though Emanuel Wilson would presumably take over No. 1 RB duties. As it is, Holani has gotten involved on offense in each of Seattle's contests so far, combining to produce 42 yards on 12 carries and two yards on one reception. The Commanders have been decimated through the air this season, but they haven't surrendered a rushing touchdown so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Holani appears to be settled in as Seattle's No. 3 backfield option heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. Holani logged 10 yards on three carries against Washington in Week 3, but he had by far his best game of the season as a pass catcher, recording five receptions on five targets for 48 yards. Both Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson seem to be firmly ahead of Holani in the competition for carries, so work as a receiver will likely be the key to Holani being able to make an offensive impact. The Chargers haven't been hurt much by RBs as pass catchers, yielding just 4.37 yard per target to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Holani is on the 2026 fantasy radar with Kenneth Walker III no longer on the Seattle roster and Zach Charbonnet (ACL) in doubt for the early portion of the season. Holani will compete with rookie Jadrian Price and Emanuel Wilson for touches while Charbonnet is sidelined. The 2024 UDFA has 25 carries and three targets to his name through two NFL seasons. Price figures to get the first shot at lead back duties and, even if forced into a few starts in Seattle's run-friendly offense, Holani would be working in a committee and no more than a deep league flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tank Bigsby managed just one carry for the Eagles in Week 1. Bigsby rushed once for three yards in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. Meanwhile, fellow backup Will Shipley garnered three total touches for 12 yards. Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans.  Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Bigsby and Will Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tank Bigsby returned to his backup role last game for the Eagles. With Saquon Barkley recovered from his stinger, Bigsby did not receive a carry in the dismal loss to the Bears. Barring injury, Bigsby will get little run in Week 4 versus the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.

player.seasonOutlook: Bigsby was acquired by the Eagles early in the 2025 season and progressively worked his way up to primary backup duties, a role he's expected to play again in 2026. Granted, it's a small sample, but Bigsby has been extremely efficient over the last two seasons. Among 48 backs with 200-plus carries during the span, Bigsby ranks first in yards after contact per attempt (2.75) and eighth in yards per carry (4.86). In fact, Bigsby has led qualified RBs in YAC each of the last two seasons. On the other hand, he hasn't been used much as a receiver (20 career targets). With overworked Saquon Barkley entering his age-29 season, Bigsby certainly has some insurance appeal, even if he defers passing-down work to Will Shipley. Bigsby, 25, is worth consideration in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mack Hollins will look to capitalize on an elevated role in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. Hollins caught four of his five targets to open the year, finishing with 51 yards, and could slide into A.J. Brown's (ankle) vacated outside role. Hollins and DeMario Douglas have the trust of Drake Maye, something that can't currently be said for Romeo Doubs, suggesting Hollins will play against a secondary that's without top corner Joey Porter Jr. Hollins' size makes him a capable red zone target, which generates upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mack Hollins will look to lead the Patriots' receiving corps in Week 4 against the Bills. Hollins gathered a season-high nine targets in Week 3, following just seven total in the team's first two games, as the Patriots continue to search for a top option without A.J. Brown (ankle) available. Drake Maye is struggling to move this offense, but Week 4 offers the potential to match the Bills' high-scoring offense. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers and an enticing 9.2 yards per target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cooper Kupp and the Seahawks travel to Arizona to take on the Cardinals in Week 2. Kupp caught two of three targets for 35 yards in a season-opening win against New England, though he would have had a bigger performance if not for a 24-yard touchdown grab that was nullified by a penalty. Of note, Drew Lock is expected to start behind center for Seattle, as Sam Darnold is dealing with a glute injury and is unlikely to suit up. The Cardinals aren't expected to field a top secondary this year, but they did a good job of holding Justin Herbert and the Chargers' offense in check in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cooper Kupp has so far had a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington. Kupp has logged just two receptions in each of the Seahawks' first two games, registering 55 yards across the four total catches. He ranks third on the team with five targets, trailing Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22) and Rashid Sheheed (nine). As those numbers suggest, Smith-Njigba is dominating looks again this season, so Kupp and Shaheed may be left to compete for scraps throughout the campaign. With that said, there may be lots of receptions to go around against the Commanders, who have given up 27 catches to wideouts through two weeks -- tied for third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cooper Kupp is coming off his biggest performance of the season as the Seahawks prepare to host the Chargers in Week 4. Kupp logged season-best marks with four catches, five targets and 46 receiving yards against Washington in Week 3, and he got into the end zone for the first time with a seven-yard TD reception. Also of note is that Kupp logged a 67% offensive snap share after being on the field for just 43% of Seattle's offensive snaps the previous week. Kupp will look to build upon the promising effort against the Chargers, who have yielded a 67.3% catch rate to wideouts so far this season, seventh-worst in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Kupp heads into his age-33 season positioned for situational targets in Seattle's run-first offense. The longtime Rams slot man appeared in 16 games for Seattle in 2025 -- his first season with the team -- and was limited to a career-low 16% target share. Kupp was a nonfactor in fantasy, clearing 12.0 fantasy points only once (16.0 in Week 2). The veteran remains a reliable short-range target, but his ceiling is very low with Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up a huge share of the targets and the likes of Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton also in the mix. Kupp is an unexciting late-round pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Mayer led the Raiders in targets with seven in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, although he turned that volume into just six catches for 32 yards. That opportunity came as Brock Bowers was sidelined following minor knee surgery, and while the third-year star isn't expected to be out long, he has yet to be cleared for Week 2. If Mayer does get the start at tight end, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in points allowed to TEs last year, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Mayer hasn't made much of an impact as the Raiders' top tight end through the first two weeks of the season, catching nine of 11 targets for 55 yards without scoring a touchdown. That role has come while Brock Bowers was recovering from minor knee surgery at the end of training camp, but with Bowers expected to return in Week 3, Mayer will see even his modest volume collapse. If Bowers' 2026 debut does get delayed further, Mayer will still be facing a Saints defense that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Mayer's stint as the Raiders' starting TE ended in Week 3 with the return of Brock Bowers, but he stayed involved in a win over the Saints, catching all three of his targets for 32 yards and his first touchdown of the season. A lack of options at wide receiver could mean Klint Kubiak will continue to lean on both his tight ends for offense, keeping Mayer relevant even with Bowers as the clear No. 1 target for Kirk Cousins. Mayer could make a splash again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs so far, but which ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justice Hill and the Ravens are at home to battle the Saints in Week 2. Hill rushed six times for 18 yards and had one catch for 10 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 win. He's established himself as the clear No. 2 RB, as his 31 offensive snaps trailed slightly behind Derrick Henry's 37. Hill should continue to see opportunities as a change-of-pace back against a New Orleans defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (38.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justice Hill and the Ravens travel to face a Cowboys defense in Week 3 that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) allowed to running backs. He tallied two carries for six yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss to the Saints. As long as Derrick Henry, who accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, is healthy, Hill's action will be limited as the No. 2 RB. However, in a contest that is expected to be high-scoring, Hill could contribute as a receiver, but he's still a risky fantasy play outside of deeper leagues.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was explosive with his five carries during Baltimore's thrilling Week 3 victory, racking up 33 yards and a 6.6 average. However, Derrick Henry handled 26 of the 31 total carries for running backs, and he remains in firm control of the Ravens' backfield. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs, and despite the possibility of Baltimore playing from ahead, Hill's involvement will continue to be limited.

player.seasonOutlook: Hill heads into his seventh NFL season positioned for a larger role following the offseason departure of Keaton Mitchell. Derrick Henry remains the team's lead rusher, but he plays only about half of the snaps, leaving plenty of opportunity for Hill, particularly in passing situations. We've seen Hill in that role recently, including a 2024 campaign in which he posted a 42-383-3 receiving line on 55 targets (11th most among backs). Of course, Hill isn't trusted with much rushing work (his career high in carries is 84), which is why he has never had a top-35 fantasy campaign in his career. The 28-year-old has a limited ceiling and would be on the flex radar in PPR formats only if Henry were to miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Calvin Ridley wasn't targeted in Tennessee's season opener and is off the fantasy radar completely heading into a Week 2 home game against the elite Eagles secondary. The veteran WR may be as low as fifth in the Titans' WR pecking order behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike. Second-year QB Cam Ward has struggled to keep any of his pass catchers consistently fantasy-relevant, let alone depth options.
outlooksByWeek.3: Calvin Ridley has drawn just two targets through two games in Tennessee's underwhelming passing game. The Titans don't have a player with more than 80 receiving yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, so Ridley's fantasy value is slim to none as a depth piece behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson. The Giants have struggled to defend WRs, but Ridley is unlikely to get enough passes thrown his way to capitalize on facing the banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Calvin Ridley has just two catches through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore. The Ravens have allowed the second-most catches to WRs this season, but Ridley remains a fantasy non-factor as a depth piece in a Titans offense that has generated the third-fewest passing yards in the NFL. Ridley is firmly behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson on the depth chart, and the 31-year-old WR has also been outplayed by Elic Ayomanor.

player.seasonOutlook: Ridley's second season in Tennessee did not go as planned, as the veteran receiver missed 10 full games and was limited to a career-low 17 receptions. He remained a featured target when healthy (seven-plus targets in his four full games), but that led to only one double-digit fantasy performance. The lost season comes after Ridley delivered consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, finishing both as a top-30 fantasy receiver. Ridley is now 31 years old and has added target competition with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson in the mix. A Year 2 leap from Cam Ward could get Ridley back into the flex discussion, but it's more likely that he's headed for a reduced role. Ridley is worth no more than a middle-round flier.

The Raiders have a lengthy track record of defensive struggles, finishing in the upper half of the league in fantasy points from the D/ST in only one of the past 15 seasons. Still, the team added LBs Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker and CB Taron Johnson during the offseason, and it does still have DE Maxx Crosby on board. There could be some streaming potential here in favorable Weeks 1 (MIA) and 3 (@NO) matchups.

Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Willis looks to rebound from a shaky debut when the Dolphins again travel west to face the 49ers in Week 2. Willis was held without a touchdown pass in his first start for his new team, and while the rushing volume was lower than expected, he scampered for a touchdown. It's a challenging road spot against a defense that allowed just 168 yards passing and no scores in their opener, but game flow should remain positive for Willis to flirt with fantasy-worthy production. Miami will likely play from behind, necessitating throws, and dropbacks will continue to lead to rushing yards when pressured.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Willis figures to labor again in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has yet to top 220 yards or complete more than 15 passes through two games, and his rushing attempts haven't been as plentiful as anticipated. Any potential late production while playing from behind has also failed to manifest, and that game script figures to repeat in Week 3 against Kansas City, a defense that's allowed only 341 passing yards, two touchdown passes, and 12 rushing yards this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Willis will be under heavy pressure when the Dolphins face the Vikings in Week 4. Willis has just one touchdown pass through three weeks and has surprisingly topped 40 yards with his legs just once. Minnesota is the heaviest blitzing team in the league, so Willis will likely need his mobility often in Week 4. Without De'Von Achane (knee) and no emerging receivers, scrambling appears his only path to production against a defense that's allowing 7.0 yards per attempt while also allowing three touchdowns with four interceptions.

player.seasonOutlook: Willis signed with Miami during the offseason and is set to start after two successful seasons backing up Jordan Love in Green Bay. Willis, a 2022 third-round pick, has very little experience (155 career pass attempts), but he was outstanding in limited work the past two seasons, completing 70 of 89 passes for 972 yards, six TDs and zero INTs (12.1 yards per attempt, 86% completion rate), while also adding major value with his legs (42-261-3) during the span. Willis played at least 80% of the snaps in three games with Green Bay and averaged 23.3 fantasy points in those outings. Willis' inexperience makes him risky and the Miami supporting cast is perhaps the worst in the NFL, but his dual-threat ability makes him a very fascinating late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacoby Brissett will look to help Arizona pull off another upset against Seattle in Week 2. Brissett was great in a season-opening win over the Chargers, throwing for 277 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. His passing score went to tight end Trey McBride, who should continue to be his top weapon as one of the league's top players at the position. The Seahawks present a tough challenge, however, as they are expected to have one of the league's top defenses and picked Drake Maye off three times in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacoby Brissett will look to bounce back from a poor performance when Arizona faces the 49ers in Week 3. Brissett recorded just 95 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception Sunday in a loss to Seattle, with that yardage being less than half of his previous low mark across any of his 16 starts for the Cardinals. Still, McBride was able to maintain his rapport with star tight end Trey McBride, as the pair connected for 41 yards and a touchdown through the air. Brissett's path to a rebound isn't an easy one, as San Francisco has given up just 11.8 fantasy points per game to QBs -- the second-fewest in the league -- through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his best game of season heading into Arizona's Week 4 clash with the Giants. Brissett threw for a season-high 280 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco while adding a TD as a rusher. His three total scores were more than the two (both through the air) he compiled over the first two weeks of the campaign. The Giants have been middle-of-the-pack statistically against the pass so far but will be without star edge rusher Brian Burns, who is out for the campaign due to a torn ACL.

player.seasonOutlook: Brissett is back for his second season in Arizona and is currently positioned as the team's probable Week 1 starter. One of the biggest fantasy surprises of 2025, Brissett reeled off nine consecutive top-12 fantasy outings spanning Weeks 6 to 15. He averaged 18.9 fantasy points across 12 starts, which was a big surprise considering his prior career high was 12.9, and that was way back in 2017. Brissett played solid ball, but he's not a major contributor with his legs (260 yards is his career high for a season). He certainly benefited from the league's pass-heaviest offense, a luxury he's unlikely to have with Mike LaFleur now calling plays. Expect the 33-year-old to regress to fringe QB2 production, and keep in mind that it's possible Arizona will turn to rookie Carson Beck at some point this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Bass continues to be busy for the high-scoring Bills' offense as they enter a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. In Week 1, Bass made three extra points and three field goals, though none were 50-plus yards. Detroit's defense, particularly the secondary, was suspect a week ago, and the Bills should score plenty, making Bass appealing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Bass will attempt to bounce back from his first miss of the season when the Bills host the Chargers in Week 3. Bass wasn't afforded a field goal try in Week 2, with Buffalo's offense finding the end zone with ease, but still provided a reasonable floor, hitting five of six extra points. The Bills' offensive efficiency could cap Bass' scoring potential, but historically, the highest-scoring kickers come from the highest-scoring teams.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Bass' opportunities have been limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup between the Bills and Patriots. Through three weeks, Bass has attempted only four field goals, though Buffalo's high-powered offense has generated 12 extra points. New England's defense remains stingy, allowing just 15 total points to opposing kickers, likely keeping Bass out of Week 4 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are on the road in Week 2 to take on Houston. The Texans have the 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to TEs, and they are last in receiving yards allowed to the position after Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox combined for 137 yards last week. Gesicki led the Bengals in catches (5), targets (7), and receiving yards (78) in Week 1, to go along with one TD. He could be primed for another big performance in what may very well be another high-scoring affair.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town in Week 4. He caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Gesicki finished third in receiving yards while catching his second TD of the young season, just one week after failing to earn a target. Jacksonville's defense ranks fifth in fantasy points allowed (7.8) and second in receptions (8) to TEs, so he could be in for another quiet day.

player.seasonOutlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kayshon Boutte was held to one catch in his Texans debut, so he doesn't profile as a viable fantasy option for Week 2 against the Bengals. Boutte may still be learning the playbook after being acquired in an Aug. 24 trade from New England, and facing a tough Buffalo secondary didn't help things in Week 1, but he will need to demonstrate greater involvement in the game plan to warrant lineup consideration outside the deepest of formats. Cincinnati's secondary played well in Week 1, as no Buccaneers WR exceeded 63 yards against them.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kayshon Boutte had three catches in his second game with the Texans in Week 2 after going without a catch in his team debut. He's probably the best downfield option in the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring), who looks likely to sit out again in Week 3 against the Colts after missing the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati. The Colts have talent in their secondary, led by CB Sauce Gardner, but they are vulnerable to big plays through the air since they often leave their cornerbacks in one-on-one coverage with receivers. Indianapolis has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL this season, so Boutte has starter-level upside in deep leagues for Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kayshon Boutte has 79 yards on nine targets through three games with the Texans heading into a Week 4 home game against the vulnerable Dallas secondary. Boutte's 8.8 yards per target (YPT) trails only Jaylin Noel's 11.2 YPT among Houston's wideouts, while Xavier Hutchinson (21 targets; 5.7 YPT) and Jared Wayne (12 targets; 5.4 YPT) haven't done much with their chances. The Texans traded for Boutte in late August, so it's possible he's being brought along slowly and could start to see his role increase, especially if Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game in Week 4. Until Boutte starts getting more opportunities, the former Patriots WR will be difficult to trust in any format.

player.seasonOutlook: Boutte was traded to the Texans in August. Reportedly a cut/trade candidate throughout most of the 2025 offseason, Boutte went on to lead the AFC champion Patriots' wide receiver room in routes and touchdowns while playing 67% of the offensive snaps when active. Despite the generous usage in a good offense, Boutte wasn't a reliable fantasy option, averaging 8.9 fantasy PPG. After seeing a career-high nine targets in Week 1, Boutte didn't clear five in a game the rest of the regular season. The 2023 sixth-round pick has finished in the range of 500-600 yards each of the last two seasons and has yet to produce a top-50 fantasy campaign. Now with Houston, Boutte will compete with Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel for Houston's No. 2 receiver role behind Nico Collins. Even if he wins that job, he doesn't figure to see enough work to find his way into the weekly flex discussion.

outlooksByWeek.2: Geno Smith may be called upon more often in Week 2 when the Jets face the Packers. He wasn't asked to do much last week as the club played with a rare lead for the majority of the game, relying on the run-something unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Green Bay's secondary is vulnerable, allowing three touchdowns to Carson Wentz to start the year. With more volume, Smith can ascend to the second tier of quarterbacks in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Geno Smith will look to be the next quarterback to take advantage of the Lions' secondary when the Jets head to Detroit in Week 3. Smith hasn't topped 250 yards through two games and has just one touchdown pass, but he is in a very favorable spot in Week 3, with Detroit having allowed three touchdown passes in each outing thus far. Smith threw 41 times in Week 2, and so long as the Lions are scoring, Smith will likely have high volume again, putting him in a position to have his best showing of the year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Geno Smith is facing an uphill battle if he hopes to match his Week 3 success when the Jets face the Bears in Week 4. Smith is coming off a sterling outing where he threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, completing 84% of his passes against the Lions. While the Bears' secondary is vulnerable in individual matchups, their overall body of work has been stout. Chicago hasn't allowed more than 153 yards over the last two weeks, with no touchdowns and three interceptions. Despite Breece Hall's likely absence, the Bears are more suspect against the run, potentially setting Smith up for a game-management approach.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith was traded to the Jets following an unsuccessful one-year stint in Las Vegas. Smith, who began his career as a second-round pick with the Jets in 2013, is in line to start, though he's a long shot for consistent fantasy production. Smith peaked with a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game with Seattle in 2022, but he has finished no better than 16th over the past three seasons. He paced the NFL in both interceptions and sacks in 2025 after finishing third in both categories in 2024 and is no longer much of a factor with his legs. The 35-year-old might bring some stability to the fantasy outlook of the team's pass catchers, but we shouldn't expect much more than that. Consider Smith only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference matchup in Week 2. The rookie third-round pick is doubtful to suit up with a fractured wrist sustained in the opener. Head coach Jesse Minter advised that Lane is seeking second and third medical opinions before establishing a timeline for his return. His health is something to monitor, but for now, his absence could make way for Devontez Walker (groin) and Elijah Sarratt (coach's decision).

player.seasonOutlook: Lane was selected by the Ravens in the third round of April's draft. Lane is a tall, perimeter receiver with the biggest hands in this rookie class. He produced solid 43-525-12 and 49-745-4 receiving lines during his final two seasons at USC. Lane was rarely used in the intermediate area and struggled to produce after the catch (career 3.7 RAC is second worst in this class), but he has the frame and skill set to allow him plenty of pro potential. He'll battle the likes of Devontez Walker and fellow rookie Elijah Surratt for work behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in Baltimore's low-volume pass offense. Lane's primary value is as dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: AJ Barner is coming off a quiet season opener as Seattle heads to Arizona in Week 2. Barner logged just two catches on two targets for 13 yards against the Patriots last Wednesday, though those two receptions were tied for second-most on the squad. Drew Lock played most of that game at QB for Seattle, and he's expected to start in Week 2 with Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury. The Cardinals gave up seven catches for 90  yards to Chargers tight ends in a win Sunday, so Barner could be a key target for Lock.
outlooksByWeek.3: AJ Barner should again lead Seattle's TE corps in a Week 3 tilt versus Washington. Barner logged a healthy 56 of the Seahawks' 70 offensive snaps Sunday versus the Cardinals, but he finished with just one catch (on one target) for eight yards. Barner did boost his fantasy line considerably with a rushing touchdown, though his three catches for 21 yards through two weeks isn't going to turn many heads. Nonetheless, he could be a sneaky option for Week 3 against a Commanders defense that has already given up four receiving TDs to tight ends, tied for most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: AJ Barner will look to build upon a big Week 3 performance when Seattle hosts the Chargers in Week 4. Against the Commanders this past Sunday, Barner registered season-high marks with five catches, nine targets and 69 yards. That production was particularly notable after the third-year tight end compiled just three catches on three targets for 21 yards over the first two weeks of the campaign. Barner could find additional success against the Chargers, who rank in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to tight ends so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Barner was a solid contributor for the Seattle offense last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick worked his way to the top of the depth chart, and although his overall volume was limited (20th among TEs in targets and yards), he found the end zone seven times and finished 14th in fantasy points (21st in PPG). The 24-year-old is a serviceable, short-range target for Sam Darnold, but even with some rushing worked in, his role in Seattle's low-volume passing offense won't allow much upside. In fact, it's possible he loses some targets to second-year TE Elijah Arroyo this season. Barner is a fringe TE2, at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 2. In his first regular-season game since Oct. 20, 2024, Watson completed 16 of 22 pass attempts for 205 yards with one TD and one INT while rushing six times for 38 yards. Although his debut was uninspiring, head coach Todd Monken said he will stick with the 31-year-old as the starting quarterback after seeing enough positive glimpses on film. Watson will face another difficult matchup against Tampa Bay's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs and therefore should remain on waiver wires.
outlooksByWeek.3: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Panthers for their home opener in Week 3. He completed 24 of 30 pass attempts for 238 yards with two TDs and no INTs, while rushing seven times for 22 yards during Cleveland's surprising Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Watson led the comeback victory with scoring strikes of 55 and 17 yards, and chemistry appears to be brewing between him and the Browns' young playmakers. He'll face a Carolina defense that held the Falcons to 129 yards passing and forced three INTs and two fumbles in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Steelers on Thursday night in Week 4. He completed 16 of 30 pass attempts for 144 yards with two TDs and no INTs while adding 11 rushes for 45 yards during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Watson did a lot of damage with his legs, a growing trend as he's racked up 105 yards on 24 carries across three outings. The Browns' offense continues to surprise, but they'll have their hands full versus a Pittsburgh defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (16.9) to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson will return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020, Watson will open the season as Cleveland's starter, but he's a long shot to return to fantasy relevance. He should be considered only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Brooks will remain in the backfield mix for Green Bay against the Jets in Week 2. While Brooks took an ancillary role to Marshawn Lloyd in Week 1, Brooks still finished the game with seven rushes for 29 yards to Lloyd's 13 for 37. Brooks is also an excellent pass blocker, so he'll still get time on the field even if it doesn't convert to rushing attempts. New York dominated Tennessee in the trenches in Week 1, but they should be a lot less daunting than a staunch Minnesota front.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Brooks should continue to stay involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Brooks was a non-factor on the ground against the Jets in Week 2 (four carries for 11 yards), but he did reel in his first catch of the season for 15 yards. The fourth-year running back should remain on the field for passing-situation plays moving forward, especially since he served that role last season even with Josh Jacobs on the field. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's been tough on RBs so far this season, allowing a top-10 16.3 PPR points per game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Brooks will remain an option in Green Bay's crowded backfield against the Buccaneers in Week 4. Brooks failed to register a carry and caught his sole target for four yards in a Week 3 loss to Atlanta, but he did log his third straight game with a 40-plus percent snap share on offense. The fourth-year running back's consistent usage on late downs as a pass catcher and a blocker makes him a valuable asset to the Packers, but not to fantasy managers at this point in the year. Tampa Bay has allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) but the sixth-highest receiving yards (165) to RBs on the year.

Despite not recording a touch to date, Isaiah Davis could have meaningful touches in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. Breece Hall (thigh) seems unlikely to play, elevating Braelon Allen to the lead back role with Davis as a secondary option. Allen hasn't shouldered a heavy load his entire career, having double-digit carries just three times, all during his rookie 2024 season. The Bears are allowing a generous 4.9 yards per carry, so even a handful of rushes for Davis could yield positive results.

outlooksByWeek.2: Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1 for the Giants, but that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, third-string running back Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly.  Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Harris does suit up in Week 2, he will be facing a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.4: Najee Harris turned back the clock in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Harris rushed nine times for 52 yards, and may have seized the backup running back job away from both Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely heavily on the running game in Week 4 versus Arizona, though Cam Skattebo remains atop the depth chart. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jauan Jennings will aim to make more of his opportunities as the Vikings take on the Bears in Week 2. Jennings garnered just one target against the Packers in Week 1, and he was unable to convert it into a reception. The veteran was still on the field for almost half of the offensive plays, which keeps him as the WR3 moving forward. He'll look to get his first catch of the season against a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jauan Jennings will hopefully return to action as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jennings sat out in Week 2 due to personal reasons, so his practice availability this upcoming week should dictate whether he plays at the Bucs. The former 49ers wideout has yet to record a catch this season, but he played almost 50 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 1. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers so far this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jauan Jennings will look to expand on his first catch of the year as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Jennings brought in one of two targets for one yard against the Buccaneers in Week 3, which is promising given that he was out due to personal reasons the previous week. The veteran should continue to operate as Minnesota's No. 3 option at wide receiver moving forward, but Justin Jefferson's injury does have a bearing on Jennings' usage. Miami has allowed a top-five 24.2 fantasy points per game to WRs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Jennings signed with the Vikings in May. The 2020 seventh-round pick was a situational player during his first three pro campaigns in San Francisco prior to breaking out with a 77-975-6 receiving line and 27th-place finish in fantasy PPG in 2024. He dipped quite a bit statistically in 2025 and failed to produce a single top-10 fantasy week, but did score nine touchdowns (sixth among WRs) in a good Niners offense. The 29-year-old will now file in third on the Minnesota depth chart behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. He's headed for a big dip in targets and, especially with Kyler Murray under center, won't be a consistent fantasy option. He's barely worth late-round consideration.

The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

outlooksByWeek.2: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to face the Texans for a Week 2 tilt. He was highly efficient with his touches in the season-opening win, tallying five carries for 20 yards while catching all three targets for 30 yards. Perine was the only other running back to record a carry, so his status as the No. 2 RB is not in question. Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, but it surrendered 409 total yards of offense in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with an illness that forced him to miss two days of practice, he was active in Week 2 and recorded two carries for six yards and caught his lone target for 16 yards during Cincinnati's win over the Texans. With backfield mate Chase Brown handling 23 total touches, Perine's limited involvement on offense makes him a solid fantasy insurance policy, but nothing more. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 28th in rushing yards (233) and 29th in receiving yards allowed (97) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Samaje Perine and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. He rushed three times for nine yards and caught one of three targets for five yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 Week 3 loss. Lead back Chase Brown handled 13 carries, so Perine is firmly established as the No. 2 option and primary passing-down option out of the backfield. Jacksonville's defense ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (17.2) to RBs, and it has surrendered just one rushing TD to the position through three contests.

player.seasonOutlook: Perine is expected to resume his role as Chase Brown's primary backup in Cincinnati. The veteran back played 31% of the Bengals' snaps last season, totaling 84 carries and 21 targets. He cleared 400 total yards for the fifth consecutive season, though he has yet to reach 200 touches in a single season in his career, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. The 30-year-old has reached double-digit fantasy points three times over the last two seasons and would require a Brown injury in order to flirt with flex appeal. He can be left on waivers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malachi Fields tied for third on the Giants in targets in Week 1. Fields caught two passes for 25 yards on four targets in his debut. Only Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely had more targets. The Giants are rather thin at wideout behind the aforementioned Nabers, and Fields is a huge target at 6-4, 225-lbs, so expect him to continue to be a decent contributor to the revamped offense. In Week 2, the G-Men will face a Rams defense that allowed 205 passing yards and three passing scores in a lackluster season-opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malachi Fields finished third in receptions and second in targets for the Giants last game. Despite seeing increased involvement, Fields caught just two passes for just 30 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Fields will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malachi Fields has two catches in each of his first three NFL games for the Giants.  Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 30 yards in any single contest.  Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Fields as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Fields was selected by the Giants in the third round of April's draft. One of the biggest and strongest receivers in this rookie class, Fields figures to work as a perimeter, vertical target in the pros (career 13.3 aDOT during 49 collegiate games). Fields, who dropped just seven passes in college, handled a target share of, at least, 20% and air yard share of, at least, 30% during each of his final three collegiate seasons (two at Virginia, one at Notre Dame). Fields will battle Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton for New York's No. 2 receiver gig behind Malik Nabers. The rookie is a fine late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Elliott was perfect on all four of his kicks in Week 1 for the Eagles. Elliott connected on a 33-yard field goal as well as three extra points in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. In Week 2, Elliott will face a Titans squad that allowed a plethora of points last season. Tennessee gave up an average of 28.1 points per clash in 2025, which was 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Elliott nailed a 58-yard field goal in Philadelphia's last game. Elliott has not missed a kick through two games for the Eagles, connecting on two field goals and six PATs. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears squad allowing 23 points per contest, which is in the middle of the pack thus far this NFL season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Elliott did not attempt a field goal last game for the Eagles, as the offense was stymied in the 27-7 loss to the Bears. Elliott did hit his lone extra point, though has now made just two field goals in three contests thus far this season. In Week 4, Philadelphia will face a Rams squad allowing 21 points per tilt, which is tied for 13th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Oronde Gadsden didn't have a big role in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, sitting third in snap share at tight end behind Charlie Kolar and David Njoku while catching both his targets for 32 yards. Njoku was the more productive receiver and Kolar by far the best blocker of the group, making it tough for Gadsden to find a niche in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme despite his impressive numbers as a rookie. Gadsden faces an additional challenge in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that finished third in PPR points per game allowed to TEs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Oronde Gadsden hasn't logged much volume to begin the season, with just four targets through two games, but he's caught all four for 50 yards and scored his first touchdown of 2026 in the Chargers' loss last week to the Raiders. The second-year tight end's usage could increase significantly in the coming games. Both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar left the Week 2 loss to Las Vegas with injuries that are expected to land them on injured reserve, leaving Gadsden as the only healthy TE on the roster. He doesn't have the blocking skills of his veteran teammates, which could limit how much OC Mike McDaniel is willing to put him on the field, but Gadsden's workload will still increase almost by default unless the team is able to find immediate help from outside the organization. He'll face a Bills defense in Week 3 that ranks in the bottom 10 in catches and receiving yards allowed to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Oronde Gadsden didn't get a significant increase in his pass-catching assignments in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, despite injuries to Charlie Kolar and David Njoku. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel prefers to have his tight ends block, which is not Gadsden's forte. While he saw a season-high 36 offensive snaps in Week 3, he only got three targets from Justin Herbert and failed to catch any of them. There still isn't any real competition for Gadsden on the roster at tight end, but fullback Alec Ingold ended up being the player who benefited most from the absences of Njoku and Kolar. Gadsden will try to prove to his new OC that he has more to offer in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Gadsden's rookie season was quite the roller coaster. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't get much early run prior to exploding for 29.4 fantasy points in Week 7 and 18.7 points in Week 8. He went on to score one touchdown and average 6.2 fantasy PPG the rest of the season, never clearing 12.2 points in a single outing. Gadsden finished the season eighth or better at the position in end zone targets, aDOT, YPR, YPT and YPRR. The 23-year-old's second-half fall is concerning, and he now enters Year 2 set to compete for work with newcomer David Njoku and Charlie Kolar. It's still possible Gadsden emerges as a featured target in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, but consistent fantasy output may be tough in an offense that figures to spread the ball around. Gadsden is only worth stashing in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.3: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Antonio Williams finished third in targets for the Commanders last game. Williams caught just two balls on four looks, though, en route to only 15 yards receiving. Williams caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Nailor didn't make much of a splash in his Raiders debut, catching three of five targets for 27 yards in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Tre Tucker and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, figure to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Nailor isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Nailor has had a quiet start to his Raiders' tenure, catching four of eight targets for 36 yards through two games without a touchdown. He hasn't been able to get on the same page as quarterback Kirk Cousins, even though the two were together in Minnesota for the first two years of Nailor's career, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Nailor seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Nailor has yet to earn much of a role as a pass catcher through his first three weeks as a Raider. While the fifth-year wide receiver does the kind of grunt work as a blocker that keeps him on the field, he's seen only 11 targets from Kirk Cousins and caught just five of them for 52 yards and zero touchdowns. With Brock Bowers making his season debut in Week 3 and immediately reclaiming his spot as the team's top target, Nailor's path to meaningful volume got even narrower. He faces a difficult task in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nailor signed with the Raiders and will battle the likes of Tre Tucker and second-year receivers Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in Las Vegas' new-look offense. Nailor was a rarely used commodity during his first four NFL seasons, all with the Vikings. The 2022 sixth-round pick totaled a 69-1,066-11 receiving line and never reached 30 catches or 450 yards in a single season. In fact, he's yet to clear six targets in a game. The 27-year-old very well could lock down a starting job in Las Vegas, but he's a long shot to make the big leap to consistent fantasy output in his fifth professional season. He's no more than a late-round wild card in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the Patriots for a Week 2 road clash. He completed 24 of 40 pass attempts for 221 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for minus-3 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory over the Falcons. The Steelers attempted 41 passes compared to just 21 rushing attempts, as Rodgers connected with seven different receivers on the day. They'll face a tougher test on the road against New England's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.3) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the division-rival Bengals in Week 3. He threw for 187 yards (23-for-39) with no touchdowns and one INT and lost one of his two fumbles during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Cincinnati has been somewhat stingy against opposing QBs, allowing 20.2 fantasy points through two outings (15th) despite giving up 353 passing yards versus Houston in Week 2. The Bengals are the only defense without an interception to this point, but they're also the only team that has yet to surrender a passing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He's coming off easily his best outing of the young campaign, throwing for 292 yards (19-for-34) with three TDs and one INT while rushing three times for 10 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Rodgers spread the ball around to nine different receivers, finding Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek for his three scores. He'll face Cleveland's 16th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.9) per game to QBs as the Steelers look to improve to 3-1 in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

The Cowboys underwent a major roster overhaul and finished on a massive cold spell defensively late last season, making it difficult to get behind them as a fantasy option at the onset of 2026. Only the Jets scored fewer fantasy points for the year. The Cowboys did restock their roster during the offseason, adding Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson and Rashan Gary (among others), and they do have a Giants matchup to open their schedule. It's still better to wait and see how this unit jells before diving in, however, even from a streaming standpoint.

outlooksByWeek.3: Kaleb Johnson could continue to carve out a role as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Johnson saw a huge uptick in usage against the Jets in Week 2, logging eight carries for 32 yards. The second-year ball carrier was the most efficient of Green Bay's RBs, and he could continue to see an early-down role if MarShawn Lloyd remains inefficient. Still, Atlanta has allowed 127 rushing yards to running backs through two weeks, a top-10 mark, which could make Johnson's job tough even if he's the Packers' go-to on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaleb Johnson will seek to earn more touches as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Johnson struggled to stay involved with Green Bay playing from behind in Week 3, logging just four carries for six yards and catching one of three passes for 10 yards. The former Steeler still saw his offensive snap share increase from 27 percent in Week 2 to 36 percent in Week 3, while Lloyd's share fell in the same stretch. This could open up more opportunities in the coming weeks, but not enough to start Johnson against a Bucs defense that's allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) to RBs on the year.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was traded to Green Bay in August after his rookie season in Pittsburgh didn't go as planned. Drafted in the third round as a potential Najee Harris replacement, Johnson quickly found himself buried behind Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell and never recovered, even losing his kick returner role after a costly Week 2 blunder. He ended his first campaign with 78 yards on 29 touches. The 23-year-old will enter his second season with a fresh start and very well could get some early-season run with Josh Jacobs facing a suspension. Johnson will compete for reps with unproven Marshawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks. Keep him stashed in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Ward threw for just 140 yards in Tennessee's 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, bringing the 2025 first-overall pick's career average down to 184 passing yards per game. He's best avoided for fantasy purposes, even in multi-QB formats, for the Titans' Week 2 home game against the Eagles. Philadelphia's stingy pass defense limited Jayden Daniels to 164 passing yards and 4.8 yards per pass attempt in the Eagles' season-opening win over Washington.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Ward has been arguably the worst starting QB in the NFL since entering the league as the Titans' first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. In the first three games of his sophomore season, Ward hasn't thrown for more than 183 yards or recorded multiple touchdown passes in a game. Dynasty managers can continue to stash him on the bench for the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore in hopes of future improvements, but Ward's fantasy value in the present is negligible. The Ravens rank in the middle of the pack against the pass.

player.seasonOutlook: Ward is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an underwhelming rookie campaign, albeit under tough circumstances. The 2025 No. 1 draft pick was plenty busy as a rookie (eighth in the league in dropbacks and pass attempts), but he struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Ward was rarely a factor with his legs (more than 12 yards three times) and produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 12th. The good news is that a tough rookie year isn't overly damning for a quarterback's career trajectory, and he'll be in a better spot in 2026 with new playcaller Brian Daboll and an improved supporting cast (Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson join a now-healthy Calvin Ridley). Ward will need to run more to become an elite fantasy option, but Year 2 is the breakout season for many quarterbacks, so he's well worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Penix (knee) is expected to operate as Atlanta's starting quarterback if available for the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 59 points to the Bears in Week 1. Penix has appeared in just 14 games during his two NFL seasons, throwing for 2,757 yards, 12 touchdowns and six interceptions. While healthy last season, Penix lead the Falcons to a 3-6 record while the offense averaged 20.6 points per game. He should be in for a very favorable matchup, with Carolina's defense giving up 40 fantasy points to Caleb Williams last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Penix is slated to make his 2026 debut during the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Atlanta has struggled offensively with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand as the team's quarterbacks over the last two weeks, scoring just 16 total points while Rush and Strand accounted for seven turnovers. However, Penix led the Falcons' offense to 20.6 points per game while throwing for 220.2 yards per game when healthy in 2025, suggesting improvement could be coming. Penix will be in for a tough matchup though, as Green Bay's defense has given up just 19.2 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Penix is expected to lead Atlanta's offense into the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. The 2024 first-round pick was impressive in his 2026 debut, throwing for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in a win against the Packers. Despite playing in the same division as New Orleans, Penix has never played a game against the Saints before. Following his Week 3 performance, the expectation is for Penix to elevate Atlanta's offense by getting the ball into the hands of Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Penix is in for a relatively favorable matchup as well, with the Saints' defense allowing 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a fine NFL starter, but even if he does, his lack of rushing will limit his fantasy output. He's well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre' Harris had a quiet performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching three of six targets for 20 yards. The second-year wideout struggled along with the rest of the passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, with the exception of Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey misses time, Harris could see additional volume. In Week 2, the second-year wideout will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points allowed per game to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre' Harris caught only one pass in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but he made it count, connecting with a scrambling Justin Herbert for a 53-yard gain that set up a third-quarter touchdown. Harris has just a 4-73-0 line on nine targets through two games, but if he continues to show he can gain significant yards after the catch, he could prove to be a good fit for OC Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 2025 second-round pick will face a Bills secondary in Week 3 that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre' Harris is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. With Ladd McConkey limited by a rib injury, Harris handled a season-high seven targets and turned them into a 6-76-0 line that led the team. A second-round pick in 2025, Harris' ability to put together a breakout year will be hampered by the dysfunctional offense around him, but he appears to be close to moving past Quentin Johnston into the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Harris faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris is a Year 2 breakout candidate after flashing in a limited role as a rookie. The 2025 second-round pick quietly played 49% of the Chargers' offensive snaps, but he spent a lot of that blocking and was limited to an 8% target share. Harris is likely to open the 2026 season behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, but with Keenan Allen gone, his competition for No. 3 duties is 2025 fifth-round pick KeAndre Lambert-Smith and rookie Brenen Thompson. A potential starter in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, the 24-year-old Harris is an intriguing late-round sleeper.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Bell hopes for additional volume in the Dolphins Week 2 matchup at San Francisco. Coming off an ACL tear in November, the rookie logged a 52.7% snap share in his NFL debut, ending with a 25-yard catch on two targets. Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas dominated the targets in Miami's limited passing game, as expected given their availability throughout training camp. The 49ers' secondary doesn't appear to be one where Bell can break out, allowing just 6.4 yards per target in Week 1. Bell is worth monitoring, but he's currently off the fantasy radar.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Bell will look for a breakout opportunity in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has drawn only three targets through two weeks, resulting in one catch and a declining snap share, playing just 40% of offensive plays last week. A potential absence from Caleb Douglas (ankle) could elevate Bell to a WR2 role in a struggling offense that often throws while playing from behind. Kansas City's pass defense has been stingy, but should Douglas sit, Bell would be an intriguing high-upside option if chasing points in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Bell will hope to build on his best game of his rookie season in Week 4 when the Dolphins face the Vikings. Bell posted seven targets in Week 3 after just three in the first two weeks, playing 72% of offensive snaps with Caleb Douglas (ankle) sidelined. Bell is the Dolphins' highest-ceiling option, but the passing game hasn't thrived under Malik Willis. Likely playing from behind, Bell could excel against a secondary that has misleading stats thanks to a Week 2 monsoon in Chicago that shut down the passing game, but Bell needs to turn potential into production before earning fantasy trust.

player.seasonOutlook: Bell was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. The heaviest receiver in this rookie class at 222 pounds, Bell is a perimeter, possession target who increased his production in each of his four seasons at Louisville. That includes a 72-917-6 receiving line in 11 games last season, though he did tear his ACL in December. The injury could lead to a slow start to his NFL career, but considering he's joining a Miami offense devoid of playmakers, he also has a path to pacing the team in targets as a rookie. Bell could find his way to fantasy relevance if healthy and if Malik Willis plays well, but there are enough concerns that he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ray Davis remains largely uninvolved in the Bills' offense entering a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. He played more snaps on special teams (six) than on offense (five) in Week 1, and as long as James Cook remains healthy, Davis is an insurance policy more than a viable flex consideration. Davis' snaps would be further limited if RB Ty Johnson is able to suit up after missing Opening Week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ray Davis has limited involvement in Buffalo's offense entering Week 3 against the Chargers. Through two weeks, Davis has logged one carry and no targets as James Cook's primary backup, making his only contribution on kick returns. Facing a defense that's allowing just 2.98 yards per carry and with no clear path to an uptick in opportunities, Davis is an insurance policy for Cook managers only.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ray Davis hasn't recorded a carry in consecutive weeks or a reception all season as the Bills get set to face the Patriots in Week 4. Davis logged a total of 16 offensive snaps all season, with Ty Johnson's return as a passing-down back further hindering Davis's hope for work. He remains solely an insurance policy for James Cook against a defense allowing 4.2 yards per carry.

player.seasonOutlook: Davis is back as the primary insurance option behind Bills' feature back James Cook III. The 2024 fourth-round pick is one of the most valuable backups in fantasy, but flies a bit under the radar due to a very small game-day role when Cook and passing-down specialist Ty Johnson are both healthy. That's been the scenario most of the last two seasons, but we've seen Davis play more than half of Buffalo's snaps in three games. During those outings, Davis averaged 21.0 touches, 130.3 yards and 19.4 fantasy points per game. The 26-year-old has no standalone value, but he'll leap into the RB2 mix should Cook miss time, which makes him worth stashing on the end of your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylin Noel finished second on the Texans with 53 receiving yards in the season opener despite being targeted just twice. Noel will need to earn a larger role to gain fantasy relevance, but he has a chance to do so given Houston's lack of a clear No. 2 WR behind Nico Collins. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte combined for eight targets in Week 1 but recorded only 53 receiving yards between the two of them, matching Noel's yardage total.
