The 2018 second-round pick peaked with a 12th-place finish in fantasy points in 2022, but that marks his only career top-25 finish and he's been way off the fantasy radar the last two seasons, partially due to injury woes (13 missed games). Kirk doesn't have a clear path to consistent targets in San Francisco, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling also in the mix (not to mention Christian McCaffrey and eventually George Kittle). The 29-year-old will begin the season on IR and is not on the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Lock is expected to serve as Seattle's starting quarterback in Week 2 versus Arizona due to Sam Darnold's glute injury. Lock took over in the first quarter of the Seahawks' season opener and guided the team to a win, completing 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions. Lock's TD was a 45-yard connection with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who again figures to be his top target against the Cardinals. Arizona is coming off a surprising win against the Chargers, during which they limited Justin Herbert to 209 yards and an interception.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Lock could have another opportunity to lead Seattle's offense in Week 3 versus Washington. Lock started for the injured Sam Darnold (glute) on Sunday versus Arizona and threw for 235 yards with three touchdowns. Darnold is reportedly making good progress in his recovery, so it's not yet clear who will helm the team's offense in Week 3. Whichever QB gets the opportunity could be in for a big game against the Commanders, who have allowed a league-high seven passing touchdowns and have no interceptions through two weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyquan Thornton saw only one target in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, failing to bring in a deep ball from Patrick Mahomes, and that sums up his role in the passing game. The former Patriot will hit for big plays on occasion, as 11 of his 19 receptions in 2025 went for 20 yards or more, but he won't see enough volume to be a reliable contributor unless injuries open up more volume for him. Thornton gets a more exploitable matchup in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in PPR points per game allowed to WRs last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyquan Thornton produced strong numbers in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, hauling in all four of his targets for 86 yards. The fifth-year speedster is at best fifth in the pecking order for looks from Patrick Mahomes, but his role as a deep option gives Thornton some big-play potential in the right matchup, even on limited volume. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyquan Thornton is settling in as a deep option for Patrick Mahomes. After getting blanked in Kansas City's opener, Thornton has caught six passes over the last two games on seven targets, and two of those receptions have gone for 20 yards or more. He's collected 108 yards in total, and while he's still looking for his first touchdown of 2026, it would take just one defensive breakdown to free him up for a long score. Thornton's low volume will make him a risky option in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: James is an intriguing insurance stash as a candidate to work as 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't record a single touch on three snaps during a rookie campaign spent buried behind McCaffrey and a host of veterans. James wasn't utilized much as a receiver at the collegiate level and underwhelmed at last year's combine, so it's unclear what his upside will be in the pros. However, if the 22-year-old wins the No. 2 gig over rookie Kaelon Black and McCaffrey misses action, he'll be a priority add. Consider him in the final few rounds in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cole Kmet will aim to stay involved as the Bears take on the Vikings in Week 2. Kmet brought in two of three targets for 35 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers in Week 1, and he was the only tight end to record a catch. While the veteran is set to be a secondary option behind Colston Loveland this season, the high-scoring ability of Chicago could allow plenty of targets for the pair. They'll face a Minnesota defense that gave up five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cole Kmet remains a depth option as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Even though Kmet played more offensive snaps in Week 2 (69 percent) than in Week 1 (57 percent), he garnered just one target and was unable to catch it. Still, young tight end Colston Loveland has yet to do much this year, which could keep a veteran presence like Kmet relevant. He'll face a Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).
outlooksByWeek.4: Cole Kmet will remain a depth option as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Kmet started off the season hot with two catches for 35 yards and a touchdown, but he's been unable to catch his sole target in each of the last two games. The veteran tight end is still a big part of Chicago's offense, but it's to be seen if this goes beyond blocking work. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 10.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.

AJ Dillon is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. While backing up Chuba Hubbard in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, Dillon accumulated 14 yards on five total touches. He will likely struggle gaining fantasy relevance without finding the end zone, as Hubbard has a firm grasp on the Panthers' backfield. However, Dillon is in for a relatively favorable matchup against a Detroit defense allowing 4.5 yards per carry to opposing RBs through three weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Sione Vaki is poised to serve as Detroit's supplementary running back once again in Week 2 at Buffalo. While the Lions were planning to use a committee approach at RB2 this season, Vaki was the only other player at the position who saw the field behind star Jahmyr Gibbs. The third-year ball carrier recorded two rushes for seven yards and brought in his sole target for 11 yards. This makes it likely he'll be the main option behind Gibbs at least in the short term. Vaki will face a Bills defense that allowed 33.9 PPR fantasy points to RBs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Sione Vaki should remain Detroit's low-usage RB2 in Week 3 against the Jets. Vaki logged one carry for seven yards and caught one pass for 13 yards against the Bills in Week 2, showcasing that the secondary running back for the Lions is a graveyard role this year. The third-year ball carrier is still on pace to log career-high numbers given his small role so far in his career, but he's nothing more than a depth option with Jahmyr Gibbs healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Sione Vaki will remain Detroit's secondary running back option in Week 4 at Carolina. Vaki hasn't been able to carve out much of a role behind phenom Jahmyr Gibbs so far this season, but he did register a season-high six carries for 26 yards, along with another catch for 11 yards in Week 3. The third-year running back remains a depth option given the usage of Gibbs so far this season, so it won't matter much that the Panthers defense has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.

outlooksByWeek.3: Konata Mumpfield's role in the Rams' Week 3 matchup against Denver could depend on the status of Puka Nacua (hip). With Nacua sidelined Monday versus Denver, Mumpfield drew the start, but he finished with just one catch on two targets for 12 yards. Meanwhile, Davante Adams posted a massive 10-195-2 line, with no other Los Angeles wideout reeling in more than one catch. The Broncos won't be an easy matchup in Week 3, as they've held opposing WRs to an average of just 13.2 fantasy points per game this season, fourth-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Konata Mumpfield is coming off the biggest performance of his young career ahead of the Rams' Week 4 matchup in Philadelphia. Mumpfield established new professional high marks with four catches for 93 yards against Denver in Week 3, with one of his receptions going for a 48-yard touchdown. The second-year wideout logged a healthy eight targets in the loss, but important context is that Puka Nacua sat out due to a hip injury. Should Nacua be able to return in Week 4, it's reasonable to expect Mumpfield to see considerably less opportunities. Still, the Eagles have been vulnerable against wideouts and just allowed Chicago's WR duo of Luther Burden and Kalif Raymond to combine for 13 catches, 151 yards and two TDs on Monday Night Football.

outlooksByWeek.2: Seth McGowan had the only touch by a Colts RB other than Jonathan Taylor in the season opener. McGowan and fellow backup DJ Giddens are irrelevant for fantasy purposes as long as Taylor is available. Taylor handled 22 touches in Week 1 and is expected to maintain a workhorse role in Week 2 at Kansas City.
outlooksByWeek.3: Seth McGowan is locked in as the little-used backup to workhorse Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, having beaten out DJ Giddens (knee) for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. McGowan has just two carries and one target through two games. With Taylor healthy for a Week 3 home game against the AFC South rival Texans, McGowan remains a non-factor in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Seth McGowan has seven career touches heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London, four of which came in the Week 3 win over Houston. With star RB Jonathan Taylor healthy, McGowan's workload is expected to remain limited in Week 4 against Washington's stout run defense. McGowan's fantasy value is purely as a bench insurance policy in case of a Taylor injury.

player.seasonOutlook: McGowan was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. McGowan is an older prospect (25), having bounced around five schools due to an off-field issue in 2021 that led to jail time and a dismissal from Oklahoma. He slowly rebuilt his career and peaked with 1,100 yards and six TDs at New Mexico State in 2024 prior to delivering 851 yards and 12 TDs at Kentucky last season. His efficiency is hit or miss, as his career 2.65 YAC is very poor, but his 4.2 forced missed tackle rate is strong. He's been effective in the passing game, as well, so there's some hope for a pro level impact. McGowan impressed at the combine, posting the top vertical and broad jump in this RB rookie class and running a solid 4.49 40-yard dash at 223 pounds. McGowan will battle DJ Giddens for primary backup duties behind Jonathan Taylor, so it's possible he finds his way to some value as an insurance hold.

Knox enters his eighth season as a solid role player for the Buffalo offense. He is on the field quite a bit (20th among tight ends in snaps last season), but defers to Dalton Kincaid when it comes to the team's top target priority at the TE position. Even when Kincaid was sidelined last season, Knox was limited to only 3.6 targets and 6.1 fantasy points per game. Knox has never posted a top-10 fantasy campaign and has finished outside the top 30 in PPG each of the last three seasons. Even if Kincaid misses additional time, Knox will max out as a fantasy TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahan Dotson is in for a great Week 2 matchup when the Falcons take on the Panthers, whose defense just allowed 12.4 yards per completion last week. Dotson played 38 offensive snaps during Atlanta's Week 1 loss, out-snapping Olamide Zaccheaus and rookie Zachariah Branch, who each logged 18 snaps. Additionally, he trailed only Bijan Robinson and Drake London in targets, despite only receiving three. Regardless, Dotson should be in for a phenomenal Week 2 matchup after Carolina's defense gave up 59 points and eight total touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as Atlanta's No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has allowed just 8.3 yards per completion this season. Despite Dotson clearly operating as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout this season, he's had little fantasy value, in large part due to the problems at quarterback. With Michal Penix set to return in the Week 3 matchup, Dotson could be more relevant but will likely remain overshadowed by Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson. Dotson could find the end zone, however, as the Packers' defense has already allowed three touchdowns to wideouts in two games, which is tied for the fourth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite playing the second-most snaps amongst Atlanta wide receivers this season (137), Dotson has managed to catch just four of 11 targets for 41 yards. He's clearly behind Bijan Robinson and Drake London in the Falcons' offensive game plan and will likely struggle finding fantasy value without a touchdown. Additionally, Dotson is in for a difficult Week 4 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's allowed just 6.5 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Singleton was selected by the Titans in the fifth round of April's draft. He is a big, versatile back with terrific speed who can contribute as a rusher, receiver, blocker and returner. While working in a committee with fellow rookie Kaytron Allen at Penn State the past four years, Singleton was effective after contact (3.46 YAC is sixth best in this RB rookie class) but struggled with elusiveness (8.0 forced missed tackle rate is worst). He was solid as receiver (102-987-9) and returner (class-high 1,138 kick return yards) during his 53-game tenure. Singleton will open his career behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears, but would make for an interesting waiver add in the event of a Pollard injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colby Parkinson will aim to be more productive when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Parkinson led Los Angeles tight ends with 47 offensive snaps in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he caught just one pass for six yards. The Rams had three other tight ends log at least 12 offensive snaps in the contest, so the week-to-week individual production among that group could vary widely throughout the season. The Giants held Dallas' starting tight end, Jake Ferguson, to just two catches for six yards in Week 1, so Los Angeles' tight-end corps could have trouble as a whole.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colby Parkinson has had a quiet start to the season heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. Parkinson logged just one catch Week 1 and followed that with a 2-15-0 receiving line on Monday Night Football. Meanwhile, fellow TE Terrance Ferguson put up a 6-54-1 line, proving that there's room for players at the position to thrive with QB Matthew Stafford -- though who that tight end is could vary on a week-to-week basis. Denver was burned by Travis Kelce for 71 yards in Week 1 but held Jaguars TEs to just 24 receiving yards in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Colby Parkinson is uncertain to be able to play in the Rams' Week 4 clash against the Eagles due to a shoulder injury. Parkinson suffered the injury in Week 3 against Denver and finished the game with no catches on one target. Meanwhile, veteran Tyler Higbee put up a strong 8-62-1 line and could be poised for more opportunities even if Parkinson does end up playing. Philadelphia has been tough on tight ends this season, giving up just 3.0 fantasy points per game to the position, second-best in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Parkinson is set to resume his role in the Rams' TE committee. The 2020 fourth-round pick was a part-time player early last season, but graduated to a much larger role in the second half. In fact, from Week 10 on (12 games, including the playoffs), Parkinson averaged 5.0 targets and 12.1 fantasy points per game, scoring nine touchdowns along the way. He finished the regular season with career-high marks across the board, which included his first top-35 fantasy campaign (17th). If Parkinson carries his increased role into 2026, he'll be a sneaky fantasy option, but the problem is that he needs to fend off Tyler Higbee and recent second-round picks Terrance Ferguson and Max Klare for work in an offense that also includes Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Parkinson, 27, is a deep sleeper worth a look in leagues that start two tight ends.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) could start if active for the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed eight total touchdowns to the Bears in Week 1. Tagovailoa was unable to suit up last week after sustaining an oblique injury in practice, which is likely a factor in why Atlanta's offense struggled so much. He struggled in 2025, throwing for 2,660 yards and 20 touchdowns while turning it over 16 times in just 14 contests. The Falcons' offense is in for a very favorable matchup, however, as Carolina gave up 334 total yards and five touchdowns to Caleb Williams last week.

player.seasonOutlook: Tagovailoa signed with Atlanta during the offseason after spending his first six seasons in Miami. The 2020 first-round pick showed signs of life a few years ago, which included a 4,624-yard, 29-TD season in 2023, but his production and efficiency have declined since. The final straw was a rough 2025 in which he threw 15 INTs (second most in the league) in just 14 games and was benched. Tagovailoa is a nonfactor with his legs (fewer than 75 yards in four straight seasons, with zero TDs during the span) and has, in turn, never finished better than 10th in fantasy points per game (he was 33rd in 2025). Even if Tagovailoa starts in Week 1, he's unlikely to be anything more than a fringe QB2 in fantasy and figures to eventually lose work to Michael Penix Jr. (recovering from a torn ACL). Tagovailoa is way off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emari Demercado filled in for the injured Malik Davis as the backup in Week 1, but barely had an impact for the Cowboys. Sitting behind starter Javonte Williams, Demercado had just two rushes for seven yards. Demercado should continue to occupy the backup role in the short term, though his opportunities should remain limited.  In Week 2, Demercado will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emari Demercado continues to play backup to Javonte Williams following the Malik Davis injury, but Demercado has had a marginal role through the first two games for Dallas. Demercado has five carries for a combined 15 yards behind Williams. Even if he receives a few extra touches, Demercado will have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL.

Demond Claiborne is set to be a secondary option at running back once again as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Claiborne did not log a carry as one of Aaron Jones' backups against the Bears in Week 2, but he did reel in his single target for two yards. Still, the rookie running back will remain a depth pick against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Demond Claiborne will remain a secondary option at running back once again as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Claiborne saw his first carries of the year in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, totaling three for just one yard. The rookie looks to be in a role opposite of DeeJay Dallas as Minnesota's secondary RB option, with veteran Aaron Jones holding full control while Jordan Mason is out. Claiborne will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs on the year.

player.seasonOutlook: Claiborne was selected by the Vikings in the sixth round of April's draft. Claiborne is an undersized back who struggled badly with efficiency during his four seasons at Wake Forest. On 558 career carries, Claiborne averaged 4.66 yards per attempt (second worst in this RB rookie class), 2.68 yards after contact and produced 5-plus yards on a class-low 32% of his carries. Also not much of a factor in the passing game, Claiborne may be limited to change-of-pace/return work in the pros. He'll open his career as a depth player behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason.

Allen was selected by the Commanders in the sixth round of April's draft. Allen has a good size and a solid efficiency profile, having ranked seventh in this rookie class in YAC (3.35) and 10th in forced missed tackle rate (4.5) during his four seasons at Penn State. Though he out-carried fellow draft prospect Nicholas Singleton in all four seasons at PSU, Allen was less involved as a receiver (career 70-490-4 line, including a weak 5.1 YPT) and doesn't figure to get much run as a receiver in the pros. Allen is a long shot as a sixth-rounder, but he's a name to monitor considering the state of the Washington backfield (Rachaad White, Jacory Croskey-Merritt). If Allen impresses during the offseason, he could sneak onto the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Shipley managed just three touches for the Eagles in Week 1.  Meanwhile, fellow backup Tank Bigsby had just one carry for three yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Will Shipley managed nine touches for 29 yards in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Shipley and Tank Bigsby would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge, as the latter had 15 touches and a touchdown to outpace Shipley. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears run defense allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Stevens missed a field goal and an extra point in Week 1 for Washington. The Commanders lost by two points, making the misses all the more glaring. Stevens will have a chance to rebound in Week 2, though, as Washington faces a Dallas squad that allowed the most points in the NFL last season, and looked no better in their season opener versus the Giants. Dallas lost an ugly 28-20 affair to the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Stevens missed his second field goal of the season last game for Washington. Stevens did make two other field goals as well as both of his PATs, but the Commanders offense is not a pretty option for a fairly shaky kicker heading into a brutal Week 3 matchup versus Seattle. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per contest thus far this season, which is second in the NFL. In addition, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels is unlikely to play for the Commanders after dislocating his elbow.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drew Stevens connected on an impressive 57-yard field goal in Washington's 33-31 win over the Seahawks last game. However, Stevens also missed an extra point, and has now missed four kicks through three outings. Stevens has a big leg but could be on thin ice with a few more misses. He should have ample opportunities in Week 4 versus the Colts, though. Indianapolis is allowing 30.3 points per tilt, which is 30th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Troy Franklin had a small role in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City, failing to catch his only target and gaining five rushing yards on one jet sweep. By contrast, Pat Bryant led the team with six targets and seems to be emerging as Bo Nix's most comfortable security blanket and the No. 3 receiver behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton. Better days will be ahead for the Denver passing game, but Franklin has some work to do to earn meaningful production. He'll face a Jaguars defense in Week 2 that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Midway through the 2025 season, Franklin appeared well on his way to a Year 2 breakout. The 2024 fourth-round pick entered Denver's Week 12 bye with five touchdowns and a team-high 81 targets (22% share). He was demoted during the week off, however, and ended up with just 24 total targets (a 9% share) over his final seven games, including the playoffs. In total, Franklin finished a respectable 41st among receivers in fantasy PPG, but the 23-year-old's demotion, coupled with Denver's offseason acquisition of Jaylen Waddle, means he's nowhere close to the fantasy radar. Franklin will battle Pat Bryant, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. Ignore him on draft day.

The rebuilding Dolphins are woefully lacking in talent on both sides of the football, and they're coming off a season in which they tied for 21st in fantasy points from the D/ST. An opening-week matchup against the Raiders could make them a viable streaming choice -- though that's directed more at you 12-, 14-team and Knockout managers ? but there's little else to like here, especially with one of the toughest overall schedules in the league ahead.

Smith heads into his second NFL season set to compete with rookie Emmett Johnson for No. 2 duties behind new Chiefs' lead back Kenneth Walker III. Smith played just 17% of the Chiefs' offensive snaps as a rookie and had nearly as many targets (35) as he did carries (44). The seventh-round pick wasn't overly effective (3.43 yards per carry, 4.9 yards per target) and was able to reach double-digit fantasy points only once (13.1 in a Week 7 blowout win). The undersized 23-year-old would likely share the backfield even if Walker were to miss time, and he has minimal fantasy appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jack Bech was the only Raiders wide receiver to make much of a difference in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, catching three of four targets for 23 yards and a touchdown. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker, produced very similar numbers in terms of receptions and receiving yards. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, figure to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Bech will look to continue building chemistry with Cousins in Week 2 against a Chargers secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jack Bech has been unable to escape a supporting role in the Raiders' offense to begin his second NFL season. Through two games, the 2025 second-round pick has a 5-48-1 line on just six targets, volume that will make it very difficult to make a consistent impact. Bech had to watch journeyman Cody White come off the practice squad and catch two red-zone TDs in a Week 2 win over the Chargers, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Bech seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.

player.seasonOutlook: Bech is a candidate for a Year 2 leap after an underwhelming rookie campaign. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 36% of Las Vegas' offensive snaps and cleared three targets in a game only twice. He failed to find the end zone while predominantly working as a short-range target. Bech will now compete with the likes of Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in a new-look offense led by coach Klint Kubiak and, at some point, No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is likely headed for a larger role in his second season and is worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darius Slayton could make his Colts debut in Week 3 against the Texans. The veteran WR signed with Indianapolis after Alec Pierce aggravated a heel injury. Slayton is likely to fill Pierce's role as a field stretcher in one of the league's least impressive WR rooms. The 29-year-old wideout has a career average of 15.0 yards per catch and has exceeded 500 receiving yards in six of seven previous NFL seasons. Slayton could eventually produce the occasional big play, but he's best avoided in Week 3 since he still needs to learn the playbook and is facing a stout Texans secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darius Slayton has a chance to make his Colts debut in Week 4 against the Commanders in London. The former Giants WR was inactive in Week 3 after signing with Indianapolis in the wake of Alec Pierce's heel injury, which landed Pierce on IR. Slayton brings similar field-stretching capabilities to Pierce, as Slayton has a career average of 15.0 yards per catch and has topped 500 receiving yards in six of seven previous NFL seasons. If Slayton gets the green light, he would be a viable deep-league flier given his big-play potential against a Commanders defense that has allowed the third-most yards to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Andre Szmyt and the Browns are on the road to square off against the Buccaneers in Week 2. He finished Cleveland's 34-10 loss a perfect two-for-two on kicks, making a 26-yard field goal and connecting on his lone PAT. Tampa Bay gave up 33 points last week, but that was to an elite Bengals offense that isn't even in the same realm as the Browns. Szmyt should be left on waiver wires as long as Cleveland continues to struggle to create scoring opportunities.
outlooksByWeek.3: Andre Szmyt and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3. He remained perfect through two games by connecting on all three of his field-goal attempts and both PATs to help Cleveland upset the Buccaneers 23-19 in Week 2. Szmyt drilled field goals of 34 yards (twice) and 50 yards, his first score from 50 or more in limited opportunities. He's proven to be reliable, but more is needed from the Browns' offense to say he's an every-week starter. After giving up a whopping 59 points in their season opener, Carolina's defense allowed just three points to the Falcons in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Andre Szmyt and the Browns host the Steelers for a divisional tilt between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Szmyt improved to 6-for-6 on FGAs and 4-for-4 on PATs across three contests in 2026. The Browns rank 24th in scoring at 18.0 points per game, but despite his perfect mark thus far, Szmyt should be considered a risky start in fantasy with other options available.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chad Ryland enters Arizona's Week 2 matchup against Seattle as the NFL's co-leader in field-goal makes. Ryland converted four of five FG attempts in a Week 1 win against the Chargers, matching his 2025 season-high mark for field goals in a game. However, the veteran kicker had just 25 FG makes last year, so it may not be wise to expect such volume on a weekly basis. The Seahawks don't figure to provide Ryland with as many scoring opportunities, as they led the NFL with just 17.2 PPG allowed during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chad Ryland will hope for Arizona's offense to find more success in Week 3 against San Francisco. The Cardinals managed just seven points Sunday in a loss to Seattle, and Ryland's only scoring opportunity was a successful extra point on that score. He was much more active in Week 1, when he made four of five FG attempts and both PAT tries. The 49ers have given up an average of only 10.0 points through two games, so Ryland may see limited opportunities again in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chad Ryland heads into Arizona's Week 4 matchup versus the Giants having gotten off to a strong start to the campaign. Ryland made all three FG tries and all three point-after attempts this past Sunday against San Francisco, with his longest kick coming from 49 yards. Though he's yet to convert from 50-plus yards out this season, Ryland has been solid in going 7-for-8 on FG tries and 6-for-6 on PATs. However, his opportunities may be limited against the Giants, who have somewhat remarkably not given up a field-goal conversion through three contests this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Tolbert signed with Miami after spending his first four NFL seasons in Dallas. The 2022 third-round pick has a path to a substantial offensive role, with Malik Washington and rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas as his top competition for snaps and targets. We have seen Tolbert as a near-full-time player in a much better offense and he wasn't much of a fantasy option. That came in 2024 when he played 76% of the Cowboys' offensive snaps. He found the end zone seven times, but was held to 610 yards and finished 54th among receivers in fantasy PPG. Tolbert played a reduced role last season and his 203 yards were the fewest since his rookie season. The 27-year-old has very limited upside and isn't worth much late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joey Slye is unlikely to get many kicking opportunities in Week 2, when Tennessee's underwhelming offense faces the ferocious Eagles defense. The Titans generated just 195 yards of total offense in their 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, and Tennessee was a bottom-three team in both yards and points per game last season, while Philadelphia gave up the fifth-fewest points in 2025. Slye isn't known for his accuracy, either, so he isn't worth using in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joey Slye has been limited to two or fewer field-goal attempts in 12 of his last 13 outings for the Titans, who continue to have one of the league's worst offenses. After averaging 16.7 points per game last season, Tennessee is scoring 15.0 PPG heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants. It's a favorable matchup on paper since the Giants are banged up on both sides of the ball, but MetLife Stadium tends to have some of the least-favorable weather conditions for kickers, and Slye's upside will continue to be capped by the Titans' inability to consistently move the ball on offense. There are better kicking options available for fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.4: Joey Slye missed his only field-goal attempt in tough conditions against the Giants in Week 3, and his opportunities figure to remain limited in Week 4 at Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing 26.0 points per game, but Tennessee's underwhelming offense rarely gets into scoring range, which is why Slye has attempted at least three field goals in only one of his last 14 games. Slye also has accuracy issues, as the last time he exceeded an 80% success rate on field-goal attempts was 2022.

player.seasonOutlook: Thomas was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. The LSU product is small (5'10/190), but extremely fast (4.28 40-yard dash) and figures to make his hay as a situational rusher, receiver and returner in the pros. He was limited to a 13% target share across his final three collegiate seasons (one at Mississippi State and two at LSU), having failed to clear 41 catches, 536 receiving yards or five touchdowns in any of the three campaigns. He'll battle Kalif Raymond and Jahdae Walker for work behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Thomas is unlikely to emerge into a reliable fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.4: Tory Horton is coming off his first catches of the season with Seattle set to host the Chargers in Week 4. Horton notched three catches on three targets for 48 yards in Sunday's Week 3 win over Washington, finishing as the Seahawks' third-leading pass catcher. However, his role makes for a limited fantasy ceiling at the moment, as he's logged less than one-third of Seattle's offensive snaps in each of his two games so far. The Chargers haven't done well against the pass this season, ranking 22nd in receiving yards allowed to wideouts through three weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Horton had the look of a Day 3 find by Seattle early on in 2025 prior to a season-ending shin injury suffered in Week 9. The 2025 fifth-round pick opened his career buried on the depth chart behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, but still found a way to make an impact while being limited to 46% of the offensive snaps. Though his production was volatile and he never cleared five targets in a game, he found the end zone five times on 23 targets. Despite the impressive showing, Horton's short-term outlook is dicey with JSN, Kupp and Rashid Shaheed presumably ahead of him on the depth chart. The 23-year-old's primary value is as a dynasty stash.

Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' roster, but is not expected to rejoin the team. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching double-digit fantasy points only once in seven games. Aiyuk is still in his prime at 28 years old, but his role and effectiveness are currently unclear. He's off the fantasy radar.

Beck was selected by the Cardinals in the third round of April's draft. Beck is a big, experienced quarterback who started for two seasons at Georgia prior to leading Miami to the national championship game last season. Beck paced this rookie QB class in completion percentage last season (72.4%) and for his career (69.5%), while also leading this group with an 80.9 QBR and 8.4 YPA during his 55-game collegiate career. He's unlikely to offer much with his legs in the pros, however, and will begin his career behind Jacoby Brissett and likely Gardner Minshew. Beck has no short-term fantasy value, though he could very well make some starts during his rookie season. Monitor him in superflex.

A 2025 seventh-round pick, Allen is set to compete with fellow second-year back Bhayshul Tuten and newcomer Chris Rodriguez Jr. for work in the Jacksonville backfield. As a rookie, Allen played 22% of the Jaguars' offensive snaps (82% of which were pass plays), but was limited to just 33 touches and failed to find the end zone or reach 4.0 fantasy points in a single game. It's likely that Tuten will operate as the Jaguars' primary back, with Rodriguez busy on early downs and short-yardage situations, and Allen used as a passing-down specialist, same as in 2025. That said, none of the three are established as lead backs, so there's an opportunity for Allen to force his way into a larger role. The 22-year-old is worth no more than a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Sanders hopes to maintain his job when the Jets host the Packers in Week 2. Sanders secured the team's opportunities in Week 1 over Blake Grupe, finishing with eight points, more where distance matters as he made two field goals from beyond 50 yards. Assuming he's again active, a higher-scoring game could be on tap against a defense that allowed 39 points in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Sanders appears on track to serve as the Jets' kicker again in Week 3 at Detroit. Despite Blake Grupe being on the roster, Sanders has been the active option through two games, hitting four extra points and four of five field goals. Volume is questionable as the Jets' offense isn't highly efficient, and Detroit's defense has allowed just two field goal attempts while surrendering nine touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jason Sanders appears in line to handle kicking duties for the Jets again in Week 4 against the Bears. Sanders has routinely been activated from the practice squad in advance of game day and has made all five of his PATs and 5-of-6 field goals. Chicago has allowed just 17 points to opposing kickers through three weeks, and with the Jets not offering a high-powered offense, Sanders seems unlikely to provide a top-end fantasy return.

player.seasonOutlook: Randall was selected by the Ravens in the fifth round of April's draft. More specifically, he was handpicked by owner Steve Bisciotti. Randall is the biggest back in this rookie class and he possesses terrific speed (4.50 40-yard dash, 113 speed score), a combination that makes him an interesting developmental flier. A converted wide receiver, Randall had a grand total of four carries during his first three seasons at Clemson prior to posting a 168-814-10 rushing line in 2025. His experience as a receiver suggests he has big upside in that area, as well (he totaled an 84-787-5 receiving line with the Tigers). He has some 2026 insurance appeal, but he'll primarily learn the ropes behind Derrick Henry and Justice Hill in 2026, with eyes on lead-back duties upon Henry's departure. Randall will begin the season on IR.

Tonges enters his fourth NFL season with no standalone value, but as a potential fringe TE1 should George Kittle miss any time. Kittle missed seven full games last season, including the playoffs (Weeks 2-6, 17, 20). During those games, Tonges handled a 17.9% target share (6.6 per game) and posted a 34-328-3 receiving line. That works out to 11.8 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth among all tight ends last season, ahead of the likes of Harold Fannin Jr., Travis Kelce, Tyler Warren and Jake Ferguson. Kittle (Achilles) is expected to be ready for Week 1, but if he's ruled out, Tonges will be a viable replacement.

Bell was selected by the Bills in the fourth round of April's draft. Bell is an undersized, but versatile, receiver who finished 2025 second in the nation (first in this WR rookie class) in receiving yards (1,278) and, while he had a class-high 25 drops across 52 collegiate games, he was better in this area last season (five drops on 146 targets). Bell showed well at the combine, running a solid 4.40 40-yard dash and posting terrific marks in the vertical and broad jump. With DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir locked in atop Buffalo's WR depth chart, Bell will compete with Keon Coleman and Josh Palmer for work. He's only worth drafting in dynasty formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Moore and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2 as they look to improve to 2-0. On Monday, Baltimore reverted him to their practice squad, despite the receiver finishing second on the team with 53 yards on one catch. However, with Zay Flowers' (hamstring) status up in the air and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane doubtful with a fractured wrist, Moore has a solid chance of being elevated to the active roster ahead of their tilt against New Orleans. He could be a name to monitor, with WR Devontez Walker (groin) also considered questionable to play.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Moore and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 road tilt against the Cowboys. He caught one of three targets for six yards and garnered 108 yards on four kick returns during Baltimore's Week 2 loss. Moore enjoyed a slight uptick in playing time with Zay Flowers (hamstring) out, as he was on the field for 31 offensive snaps compared to 25 in the season opener. Flowers is expected to return in Week 3, but even if he remains sidelined, Moore's limited involvement on offense takes him out of any fantasy consideration.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Moore and the Ravens return home from Brazil to host the Titans in Week 4. The 33-year-old brought in his only target for a four-yard touchdown during Baltimore's 34-31 victory in Week 3, his first of the season. Moore has now had one reception in all three outings, earning him a 3-63-1 line on six targets. Tennessee's defense is vulnerable through the air, as it ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs, but Moore's limited involvement in a run-heavy offense should keep him firmly on waiver wires.

outlooksByWeek.2: Andrei Iosivas and the Bengals travel to face the Texans in Week 2. He hauled in two of three targets for 12 yards during Cincinnati's season opener, tying Ja'Marr Chase in receptions despite Iosivas garnering 21 fewer snaps on offense. However, his role is limited with Chase, Tee Higgins, Chase Brown, and Mike Gesicki all healthy. Iosivas will remain locked in as the No. 3 WR versus Houston's 25th-ranked defense in yards allowed to receivers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Andrei Iosivas and the Bengals are on the road for a Week 3 meeting versus the Steelers. He caught his only target for seven yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 victory, and it looks like that could be his norm moving forward. Iosivas played 54% of offensive snaps after playing 61% in the season opener. He's clearly behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins in the receiver pecking order and thus should remain on waiver wires in Week 3 against Pittsburgh's second-ranked passing defense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Riley Patterson's floor remains low in a limited Dolphins offense entering Week 2 against the 49ers. While he had three field goal opportunities to open the year (making two), he converted only one extra point. Field goals likely aren't going to cut it with the Dolphins defense allowing points early and often, keeping Patterson off fantasy rosters.
outlooksByWeek.3: Riley Patterson's floor remains capped by the Dolphins' limited offense entering Week 3 against the Chiefs. While Patterson has notched three field goal attempts in two straight weeks, he's attempted just one extra point in each outing. Kansas City is allowing 8.0 points to opposing kickers through two games, and that seems to be Patterson's ceiling.
outlooksByWeek.4: Riley Patterson brings limited potential in the Dolphins' low-scoring offense into a Week 4 matchup with the Vikings. Patterson has just three extra points in as many games this year while connecting on 5-of-7 field goal attempts. Minnesota's defense has allowed only three touchdowns with eight field goal attempts, and Patterson will have the benefit of kicking indoors, but it's difficult to envision a scenario where Patterson is busy in Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Stowers was selected by the Eagles in the second round of April's draft. Stowers is a converted quarterback who improved his production each of the last three seasons, peaking with a 62-769-4 receiving line in 2025. He aligned in the slot on 72% of his collegiate routes (highest among this rookie tight end class) and his career 2.38 YPRR is easily tops in this TE class. He's not much of a blocker, but he sports good speed and athleticism (he posted the best vertical and broad jumps among TEs at the combine). Stowers will have minimal fantasy value while working behind Dallas Goedert as a rookie, but he has long-term TE1 upside and will be a popular breakout candidate in 2027.

outlooksByWeek.3: Cody White is coming off the best game of his NFL career in the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers. The journeyman wideout, who followed Klint Kubiak from Seattle to Las Vegas in the offseason, came off the practice squad and caught both his targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns, not bad for a player who had just one TD in his first 31 NFL games. White's main value comes on special teams however, and his path to an increased role in the offense will get even narrower once Brock Bowers is cleared to make his 2026 debut. White will remain a dart throw for fantasy purposes in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to WRs so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cody White continues to surprise for the Raiders, catching his third touchdown in two games in a Week 3 win over the Saints. The former Seahawk, who followed head coach Klint Kubiak from Seattle to Las Vegas and knows the playbook well, has been bouncing between the practice squad and the game-day lineup, but with Jack Bech landing on IR, there's now an open spot for him to get added to the 53-man roster. White seems to have an edge on Malik Benson and Dareke Young for the vacant No. 3 spot on the wide receiver depth chart, and while he won't maintain that scoring pace, he seems to have earned the trust of Kirk Cousins as well. White will face a difficult task in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After failing to lock down a starting gig with the Bears, Steelers and Jets, Fields was traded to the Chiefs and will move forward as Patrick Mahomes' backup. That's obviously unlikely to lead to much playing time, barring a Mahomes injury. Should Fields start, he'll find his way into the QB1 discussion because of his elite rushing ability (45.1 rush rushing yards per game last season and four-plus rushing TDs in four straight seasons). In seven full games last season, Fields averaged 19.2 fantasy points, including 25 points in three of those games. He averaged 18.9 points with Pittsburgh in 2024 and 19.3 during his final two seasons in Chicago. Roster Fields in only deep superflex leagues.

Johnson was a solid find by the Giants in the fourth round of the 2024 draft, but he's headed for a reduced role this season following New York's signing of Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers' return to health. The change comes after Johnson ranked top 12 among tight ends in both snaps and routes, but 23rd in catches and 19th in yards last season. Johnson was busy near the goal line (seven end zone targets), but struggled with drops (tight end-high nine), which led to a poor 63% catch rate. Johnson finished 23rd in fantasy PPG and now may be lucky to see a target or two per game. He's well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hollywood Brown did not record a target in Week 1 for the Eagles. Meanwhile, rookie Makai Lemon was the No. 3 wideout behind DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, which included four targets in his NFL premiere. Brown looks like an afterthought heading into Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans allowed 215 yards passing and zero touchdowns through the air in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.4: Hollywood Brown has yet to catch a pass for the Eagles in 2026.  He was sidelined in Philadelphia's last game due to an ankle injury. Darius Cooper has operated as the No. 4 wideout in his stead. If Brown can suit up in Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown signed with the Eagles and he's likely to slot in either third or fourth on the team's depth chart behind DeVonta Smith, first-round rookie Makai Lemon and perhaps Dontayvion Wicks. Once a featured target in Baltimore and Arizona, Brown was more of a situational player during his two seasons in Kansas City. He barely saw the field in 2024 due to injury before handling a career-low 14.2% target share in 16 games in 2025. Brown cleared 10 fantasy points three times, but all came prior to Week 7. With Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley also heavily in the mix for targets in Philly, Brown will have to beat out Lemon and Wicks for a starting gig in order to have any chance at flex value.

Raridon was selected by the Patriots in the third round of April's draft. Raridon is a tall, blocking tight end who was barely targeted (5% share) and totaled a 48-623-3 receiving line during four seasons at Notre Dame. Most of the receiving work came in 2025, so perhaps there's some hope in that area, but he's a long shot for fantasy value any time soon, especially with Hunter Henry ahead of him on the depth chart this season.

Simpson was selected by the Rams in the first round of April's draft. Simpson was a one-year starter at Alabama and wasn't overly impressive statistically, completing 64% of his passes and posting a pedestrian 76.6 QBR. He's fairly accurate with an average arm, but he's a bit undersized and doesn't figure to move the needle a ton with his legs (62-309-2 rushing in 2025). Simpson won't see the field consistently until Matthew Stafford retires, so he's well off the 2026 fantasy radar. Keep him stashed in dynasty, especially superflex formats.

Arroyo is eyeing a Year 2 breakout after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he played a clear second fiddle to A.J. Barner. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 39% of the offensive snaps during the 13 games he was active. He cleared three targets in a game only once (five in Week 7) and his lone touchdown came on one of just two targets in Week 9. Arroyo was effective as a vertical target at the collegiate level, so he remains an intriguing dynasty hold, but the 23-year-old has a tough path to short-term fantasy relevance while stuck behind Barner in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

Flacco re-signed with the Bengals and will back up Joe Burrow this season. The veteran quarterback made six starts for Cincinnati last season and showed well, totaling 14 touchdowns and four interceptions while averaging 19.9 fantasy PPG. The 41-year-old can still sling it, but he's a nonfactor with his legs and hasn't finished a season better than 20th in fantasy points since 2014. If Burrow is sidelined, Flacco will do enough through the air to land in the QB2 discussion, but that's his ceiling.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mason Taylor will push for more involvement when the Jets host the Packers in Week 2. Taylor logged a decent 68% snap share to open the year despite Kenyon Sadiq being available but turned three targets into two catches for minus-two yards. Week 2 figures to be a more pass-heavy game script, and the Packers allowed six catches and a touchdown to the position in Week 1, but Taylor likely needs to prove he's part of the game plan before managers take notice and consider him a viable option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mason Taylor's availability for the Jets' Week 3 matchup with the Lions is uncertain due to a thumb injury that forced him to exit Week 2 early. Taylor didn't record a catch prior to exiting and has only three targets on the season, leaving him with a very questionable role. The matchup could make him a sneaky option if desperate, as Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to the position in each of their first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mason Taylor will need to overcome a thumb injury if he's to help the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears. In Taylor's absence, Kenyon Sadiq had a breakout performance in Week 3, snagging seven passes for 105 yards and a touchdown. It seems likely he'll at least share snaps if Taylor is deemed healthy for Sunday. Chicago hasn't allowed 30 yards to an opposing tight end, and when splitting the workload, Taylor doesn't profile favorably.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor was a busy man during his rookie season, playing 81% of the Jets' offensive snaps and handling a healthy 19% of the targets in 13 games. The 2025 second-round pick struggled badly with efficiency while dealing with the team's quarterback woes, ranking near the basement in catch rate (65%) and yards per target (5.4). Taylor also dropped five passes (fourth most), scored only one touchdown and finished 30th in fantasy PPG. Taylor would've been a potential 2026 breakout candidate, but that was quickly derailed when the Jets selected Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's draft. Taylor will play a role in the New York offense, but he won't see nearly enough targets to allow any sort of fantasy relevance.

outlooksByWeek.2: Noah Gray collected plenty of snaps in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, playing 55% of the offensive snaps to Travis Kelce's 71%. However, the backup tight end logged only one target, which he turned into a five-yard reception. Gray is coming off his least productive season in 2025, posting a 21-178-0 line on 37 targets. He had produced a career-best 40-437-5 line on 49 targets the year before and is capable of occasional spike games with a healthy Patrick Mahomes back under center. Gray gets a very favorable matchup in Week 2 against a Colts defense that ranked 31st in receiving yards allowed to TEs last season.

Elic Ayomanor caught an 11-yard touchdown in garbage time during the Titans' season opener. That was the only catch of the game for the 2025 fourth-round pick, and Ayomanor is expected to maintain a supporting role in Tennessee's underwhelming offense in Week 2 against the Eagles, keeping him well outside of the fantasy lineup conversation in most leagues. The Titans struggled to move the ball while the game was in doubt in Week 1 against the Jets, with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson both working ahead of Ayomanor at WR.
outlooksByWeek.3: Elic Ayomanor leads the Titans with 80 receiving yards and has the team's lone touchdown through the air this season heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants. The second-year WR's success has come despite him working as a depth option behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley. Ayomanor could earn an expanded role if he continues to make the most of his opportunities, but unless that happens, he's unlikely to find sustained success given the substantial competition for targets in one of the league's least productive passing offenses. The Giants are banged up in the secondary, but Ayomanor remains a speculative deep-league dart throw.
outlooksByWeek.4: Elic Ayomanor has drawn exactly three targets in each of Tennessee's three games ahead of a Week 4 trip to Baltimore. He remains a fantasy non-factor, even though the Ravens have given up the second-most catches to WRs. Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson each have at least twice as many targets as Ayomanor this season, and Titans QB Cam Ward is averaging just 168 passing yards per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals travel to face the Texans in Week 2. The 25-year-old rookie and former CFL receiver played nine snaps on offense and six on special teams during Cincinnati's Week 1 win. Meyers flashed with his limited opportunities, catching his lone target for 18 yards while rushing once for 10 yards. There's a chance he could leapfrog Colbie Young on the depth chart, but we'll have to see what he does against Houston's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals host the Jaguars in Week 4. The rookie receiver caught three of five targets for 29 yards during Cincinnati's Week 3 loss, stepping up with Colbie Young (knee) and Andrei Iosivas (thumb/IR) out due to injuries. Meyers tied Mike Gesicki for third on the team in receptions, though he garnered two more targets than the tight end. He's still firmly behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins in the passing game, but he's showing signs of being a reliable option in a banged-up WR room. Meyers will look to contribute against Jacksonville, whose defense ranks 26th in receiving yards allowed (527) to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones returns for his second go as Brock Purdy's backup in San Francisco after showing well in relief duties in eight starts last season. In those eight appearances, Jones completed 70% of his passes and threw 13 touchdowns to six interceptions. The 2021 first-round pick was a nonfactor with his legs (28-64-0), however, which limited him to an underwhelming 16.3 fantasy PPG. Should Purdy miss time in 2026, Jones will be no more than a fringe QB2. The 28-year-old shouldn't be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Goodson is the third backup running back already for the Cowboys this season. With Malik Davis injured and Emari Demercado deemed ineffective, Goodson had six carries for 22 yards in his season-debut versus the Ravens. However, Javonte Williams remains the undisputed starter, leaving Goodson and company picking up the scraps. In Week 4, the Cowboys will also face a rather stingy Texans run defense allowing 86.7 yards per game on the ground, which is fifth in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tommy Tremble is expected to operate as Carolina's top tight end in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. The Notre Dame product led the Panthers' tight end corps in targets (five) and receptions (three) in the Week 1 loss, though he was outgained by Darren Waller (2-28-0). Tremble could very well operate as Carolina's No. 3 receiving option going forward, as Xavier Legette saw just two targets in Week 1. Additionally, Tremble is in for a great Week 2 matchup, as Atlanta's defense allowed 19.4 PPR fantasy points to tight ends last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tommy Tremble is expected to remain the Panthers' top tight end in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Tremble was overshadowed by Darren Waller in the Week 2 win, as Waller paced Carolina's tight end corps in targets (three), receptions (three), yards (33) and touchdowns (two) Despite this, Tremble played six more Darren Waller (32 to 26), suggesting he's still operating as the Panthers' top TE. Regardless, Tremble could struggle in Week 3 against a Browns defense that's allowed just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tommy Tremble is expected to remain one of Carolina's top tight ends in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Tremble has had a solid start to the season, catching seven of 11 targets for 70 yards. Despite this, he's been overtaken by Darren Waller for the Panthers' top receiving TE, as Waller has tallied 10 receptions on 14 targets for 112 yards and two touchdowns. Regardless, Tremble should be in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 33.4 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season, the most in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.3: Demond Claiborne should remain a top supplementary option at running back as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Dallas saw an uptick in usage against the Bears with Jordan Mason landing on IR, as Dallas recorded two carries for eight yards and one catch for 12 yards. The veteran running back will likely have to compete with rookie Demond Claiborne for touches, but Dallas established himself as the second option last week. He'll face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Demond Claiborne should continue to be a secondary option at running back once again as Minnesota plays the Dolphins in Week 4. Dallas registered one carry for two yards in Week 3 against the Buccaneers. While his usage was low again, the veteran still appears slotted next to rookie Demond Claiborne in the RB totem pole behind Aaron Jones. Both could make the most of their action against a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs this year.

outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Badie was inactive for the Broncos' opener but worked into the backfield mix during Week 2's win over the Jaguars thanks to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Working as the No. 3 running back behind J.K. Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman, Badie gained just one yard on his only carry but caught two of three targets for 28 yards. Dobbins also picked up a hamstring injury in the win, and while the issue isn't expected to keep him sidelined, the veteran RB's history of injuries makes any appearance on the injury report a cause for some concern. If Badie does see a bigger role in Week 3, he'll be facing a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Badie worked as the No. 3 running back for the Broncos in a Week 3 win over the Rams, but he managed only two touches for 14 scrimmage yards. With rookie Jonah Coleman on IR, Badie doesn't have much competition for his spot, but he also doesn't pose much of a challenge to J.K. Dobbins as the primary early-down back or RJ Harvey as the main passing-down option. Badie will try to take advantage of his limited opportunities in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kevin Coleman isn't a factor in the Dolphins' limited passing game ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the 49ers. He collected just two targets in the team's opener, failing to record a catch. While Miami will be forced to throw from behind often in Week 2 and beyond, it doesn't appear as though Coleman will garner enough looks to be a fantasy consideration.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kevin Coleman remains without a catch through two games as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs. Coleman logged a higher snap share than Chris Bell, and both roles could be elevated if Caleb Douglas (ankle) is unable to play. Miami has completed only 29 passes through two weeks, and the passing game seems unlikely to sustain even a second receiver in a matchup against a Kansas City secondary that's allowing a mere 6.2 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kevin Coleman has a minimal role in Miami's lackluster passing game heading into a Week 4 matchup with the Dolphins. Coleman had a three-yard catch on four targets in Week 3 after being elevated to No. 3 on the WR depth chart due to Caleb Douglas' absence. This offense can't sustain a second receiver, let alone more, keeping Coleman far off fantasy radars ahead of a matchup with a Vikings secondary that's allowing a hearty 8.2 yards per target.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman Jr. was selected by the Dolphins in the fifth round of April's draft. Coleman is a small, slot receiver and punt returner who aligned inside on 83% of his 943 collegiate pass routes. Despite playing at three different FBS schools over the last three seasons, Coleman handled a solid 21% target share during the span and played well, catching 72% of his targets and dropping only four of 229 targets (1.7%). He posted a weak, 88 speed score at the combine, running a 4.49 40-yard dash at 179 pounds. Coleman will battle fellow rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, as well as a host of veterans for a role in a Miami offense likely to struggle to score points. He should only be drafted in dynasty.

Allar was selected by the Steelers in the third round of April's draft. Allar is one of the biggest quarterbacks in this rookie class and, while he has the arm to go with his frame, accuracy is a big concern. Allar was conservative during his time at Penn State (7.6 aDOT), but he still completed only 63% of his passes and averaged 7.4 yards per attempt. In 2025, he had the worst QBR in this rookie class prior to suffering a season-ending broken ankle. On the plus side, he could add value with his legs, as he posted a career 181-1,030-12 rushing line and his 8.3% scramble rate is second highest in this class. Allar will begin his career learning the ropes behind Aaron Rodgers and perhaps Mason Rudolph.

Williams is primed for a larger role in his second NFL season. The 2025 third-round pick had a unique rookie campaign, handling more carries (11) than he did targets (10). Williams' gadget role allowed him only 90 snaps (12%) and he was utilized only near the line of scrimmage (1.4 aDOT). The Green Bay WR rotation no longer includes Romeo Doubs or Dontayvion Wicks, but Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and fellow second-year wideout Matthew Golden remain in the mix. Williams will need to beat out one (or perhaps two) of them and start to see more downfield targets in order to land on the fantasy radar. The 24-year-old is only worth late-round consideration in deeper formats, especially since he'll open the season on IR.

outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Watkins heads into San Francisco's Week 4 matchup versus Denver with momentum on his side. Watkins played for the first time this season Sunday versus Arizona and caught both of his targets for 60 yards. That production came with No. 1 wideout Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) missing the entire second half of the contest, and Watkins' opportunities in Week 4 could logically depend upon Evans' ability to suit up. With that said, the Broncos could be a challenge for the 49ers' wideout corps as a whole given the 50.9% catch rate they've yielded to WRs so far (second-best in the NFL), though Rams star WR Davante Adams did just a 7-137-0 line on them in Week 3.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darius Cooper caught the game-winning touchdown for the Eagles in Week 2. Cooper managed just two catches for 26 yards, though one of them gave the Eagles the lead for good with precious seconds left on the clock. Cooper also tied for third on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bryce Lance is expected to play as the Saints' No. 3 wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Lance had a promising NFL debut, catching three of four targets for 42 yards. He was on the field for 62 of New Orleans' 90 offensive snaps, appearing to be the clear WR3 behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, and Tyler Shough looked Lance's way on a failed two-point conversion attempt in OT that would have won the game. While Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) remains sidelined, Lance should continue to be a valuable part of this Saints offense, especially with Shough attempting 56 passes in Week 1. Lance is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 7.8 yards per completion last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bryce Lance is expected to remain the Saints' No. 3 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite playing 78 percent of New Orleans' offensive snaps in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Lance drew just one target. He remains far behind Chris Olave and Devaugh Vele in the team's receiving corps, with his role likely diminishing further once Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns from IR. However, Lance, who ran a 4.34 40-yard dash, could find success against a Raiders secondary that's allowed 12.3 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bryce Lance is expected to remain a depth option in the Saints' receiving corps in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. The rookie from North Dakota State has operated as New Orleans' WR3 this season while Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined. Despite this, Lance has struggled to produce, catching just four of eight targets for 50 yards. He's expected to remain a depth piece behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele and will likely struggle finding fantasy value without a TD. However, Lance is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's given up 10.5 yards per completion this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Lance was selected by the Saints in the fourth round of April's draft. Trey's little brother is the lone wide receiver in this rookie class who didn't play a single snap at the FBS level. However, he was productive as a perimeter receiver at North Dakota State, posting receiving lines of 75-1,053-17 and 51-1,079-8 over the last two seasons. He's a year or so older than most of his classmates, but he dominated at the combine with terrific showings in the 40-yard dash (4.34), vertical (41.5) and broad jump (133). He has the size and skillset to handle New Orleans' No. 3 gig behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele until first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson returns from injury. Lance's primary value is in dynasty leagues.

Sarratt was selected by the Ravens in the fourth round of April's draft. Surratt is a big, perimeter receiver who hauled in 31 touchdown receptions (most in this rookie WR class) in 40 collegiate games, which includes a FBS-high 15 in 2025. His efficiency was terrific across the board, including 10.7 yards per target, 2.69 YPRR and a 72% catch rate. Surratt is an intriguing prospect, but he may not see the field a ton as a rookie with Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and fellow rookie Ja'Kobi Lane also in the mix in Baltimore's low-volume pass attack. He's best as a dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.3: Erick All Jr. and the Bengals travel to face the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After not recording a target in the season opener, All tallied two catches on three targets for five yards in the Week 2 win over Houston. He was on the field for 24 offensive snaps compared to 21 for starter Mike Gesicki, but that trend will have to consistently continue for him to even be considered in fantasy formats. With Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins accounting for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 Week 2 pass attempts, it's going to be hard to trust anyone outside of those two in the passing game, especially against Pittsburgh's second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) to TEs.

outlooksByWeek.4: Laquon Treadwell has caught all four of his targets for 81 yards over the Colts' last two games, and the 31-year-old journeyman could continue to be used as a field stretcher in Week 4 against Washington's beatable secondary in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Indianapolis signed Darius Slayton after Pierce was placed on IR, but Slayton was inactive for the Week 3 win over Houston. Slayton could take over the role currently occupied by Treadwell, and even if Treadwell maintains that role, the latter lacks fantasy appeal considering Treadwell has just five touchdown catches in 96 games, with his last score coming in 2021.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonnu Smith will look to stay involved in Green Bay's passing game at New York in Week 2. Smith was a solid option for Jordan Love in Week 1, converting two of his three targets for 50 yards. While the veteran remains an option behind Tucker Kraft, he should at least continue to be on the field and run routes. Smith will face a Jets defense that limited Titans tight ends to five catches for 35 yards in its opener.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jonnu Smith will seek to stay involved as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Smith was a solid outlet for Jordan Love in Week 3 against the Falcons, hauling in two of three passes for 16 yards. The veteran tight end has only registered catches in games where Green Bay has thrown 40 or more times, but these games seem more likely than not in the coming weeks, especially given the struggles of the run game. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a bottom-10 183 receiving yards to TEs this year.

Josh Cameron has two touchdown catches in his first three games for the Jaguars, but the rookie sixth-round pick has drawn only three targets heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. His nose for the end zone could pique the interest of managers in dynasty or keeper leagues, but Cameron isn't a viable fantasy option as long as WRs Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, and Brian Thomas are healthy. Cameron has also been contributing on special teams, both as a kick returner and in kick coverage.

player.seasonOutlook: Cameron was selected by the Jaguars in the sixth round of April's draft. Cameron is a big, strong, perimeter receiver who aligned out wide on 84% of his collegiate routes across five seasons at Baylor. Cameron's overall efficiency is underwhelming (1.58 YPRR), but he was certainly busy the last two seasons, totaling 52-754-10 and 69-872-9 receiving lines. He'll begin his career no higher than fifth on the Jacksonville depth chart behind Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter.

Benson's pro career is off to a slow start due primarily to a variety of injuries. The 2024 third-round pick was essentially splitting the Arizona backfield with James Conner last season, but he was never able to return to the field after suffering a knee injury in Week 4. He was effective prior to the injury, averaging 5.5 yards per carry, and was busy as a receiver (four-plus targets in three straight games). The 24-year-old will open the 2026 season on injured reserve and, even when healthy, he's no longer assured of a role with a new coaching staff and after the team added Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier. Benson's best days are likely ahead of him, but his only shot at 2026 fantasy relevance is a new home or several injuries above him on the Arizona depth chart.

Sanders is back as a pass-catching tight end in Carolina, though he's unlikely to see a larger share of the target pie with veteran Darren Waller now in the mix. Sanders - a 2024 fourth-round pick - flashed as a rookie with a 33-342-1 receiving line while playing 55% of Carolina's offensive snaps and handling 9.1% of the targets across 16 games. He simply didn't progress in Year 2, posting a 29-190-1 line while playing 52% of the snaps and handling a 10% target share in 12 healthy games. Sanders has been an inefficient short-range target with little goal line activity thus far (four career end zone targets), placing the 23-year-old well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.3: Johnny Mundt caught two passes in Dallas Goedert's place last game for the Eagles, and would be the next man up at tight end if Goedert cannot suit up in Week 3. Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for the clash with Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Johnny Mundt had a four-yard grab last game for the Eagles, as he is splitting tight end duties due to the injury to Dallas Goedert. Zach Ertz made his return to the Eagles, but it was not exactly triumphant. Signed during the week due to the injury to Goedert, Ertz managed just one catch for nine yards in the dismal 27-7 loss to the Bears.  Goedert's status remains very much in question for Week 4 versus the Rams. Even Goedert cannot suit up, the Rams have been rather stingy against the pass so far in 2026. Los Angeles is allowing just 171.3 passing yards per contest, which is fourth in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Whittington will look to improve upon a quiet season opener when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Whittington had just one catch for eight yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco. Still, he was the only Rams WR outside of stars Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to log a reception. Nacua and Adams stand to command most of QB Matthew Stafford's attention, so Whittington figures to compete for scraps with Los Angeles' tight ends and other depth wideouts each week. The Giants held Dallas' passing game in check in Week 1, as QB Dak Prescott tallied just 175 yards through the air, though he did toss two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Whittington (quadriceps) sat out the Rams' Week 2 win over the Giants and isn't certain to return for a Week 3 matchup against Denver. It was a missed opportunity Monday for Whittington, as top wideout Puka Nacua (hip) was also sidelined, opening the door for other WRs to take on a bigger role. Whittington was quiet in Week 1 against San Francisco with just one catch on one target for eight yards, and when both Nacua and Davante Adams are healthy, he figures to be competing with a variety of other pass catchers for targets. Should Whittington return in Week 3, he'll draw a tough Broncos secondary that has allowed a 51.6 percent catch rate to wideouts -- second best in the league -- so far this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devontez Walker and the Ravens face the Saints and their 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs in Week 2.
